title: Meta Ray-Ban update will block the most obvious loophole for disabling the privacy LED
snippet: Meta continues to crack down on malicious users disabling the privacy LED on its Ray-Ban smart glasses, this time focusing on the most obvious loophole out there. more…
fullText:
Meta continues to crack down on malicious users disabling the privacy LED on its Ray-Ban smart glasses, this time focusing on the most obvious loophole out there.

Detailed by Meta’s VP of AR, Alex Himel, on Threads, a new update is “coming” to Ray-Ban smart glasses and Meta Smart Glasses to further block users from disabling the privacy LED. 

Previously, Meta targeted users who were modifying the hardware to disable the LED, but it left the door open to an easier loophole – starting the recording and then covering the LED. While the glasses would block a recording from starting when the LED was covered, this loophole allowed users to cover the LED after the recording had already started. This new update stops the camera from recording if the light is covered.

Himel explains:

	

We have an update coming to increase the reliability of the capture LED on our AI glasses. The camera won’t start recording if the LED is blocked, but some people try to bypass this by starting a recording and then covering it up. A fix for this is starting to roll out – the camera will now stop working if the light is covered during a recording.

We’re going to keep rolling out updates like this to make sure the capture LED can reliably alert bystanders when photos or videos are being captured for someone’s gallery. Only a tiny minority of people try to get around these protections, and the fact they have to go to these lengths shows our efforts are working. We’ll keep improving and evolving our approach. 

On a dedicated privacy page on its website, Meta says that if the glasses “detect the Capture LED light was covered, physically tampered or destroyed, they’ll automatically disable the camera,” adding that “it’s that simple.” The page also goes over “tips to help you and those around you feel safe and comfortable while you’re wearing your glasses” such as turning off the glasses in “sensitive spaces” and reasoning that you shouldn’t record with glasses if you wouldn’t record with your phone. 

The page also, notably, points out that “You, and only you” can see photos and videos captured on the glasses. That’s seemingly contrary to past reports that human moderators see videos from the glasses. 

It’s unclear exactly when this next update will roll out, but it comes as smart glasses are under intense scrutiny from society, with Meta the main name in that conversation.

title: The ‘cheap smartphone era is over’ and price hikes are ‘permanent,’ bleak forecast reveals
snippet: According to the latest analyst forecasts, higher smartphone prices won’t be changing anytime soon amid a record-setting drop in shipments. more…
fullText:
According to the latest analyst forecasts, higher smartphone prices won’t be changing anytime soon amid a record-setting drop in shipments.

IDC reports that its forecast for the 2026 global smartphone market has taken a turn for the worst. Where a drop of roughly 14% was expected, that’s now up to a whopping 16.7% fall year-over-year. It’s a drop of around 200 million smartphones. The second half of the year, which we’re well into, will see the hardest hit.

Of course, the number of smartphones shipped has little to no impact on the end user, besides they might stick on their current device a bit longer.

What does have impact is pricing, with higher prices for smartphones apparently set to stick around “permanently.” The prices of memory are expected to continue going up through at least 2028 and, even after that, IDC forecasts that average selling prices will only go down by around 1-2% per year starting in 2028. In other words, next year’s smartphones will probably be even more expensive than this year’s releases, and low-end devices will only become harder to find as brands focus on the higher-end models that don’t have such thin margins.

	

As memory prices are expected to continue increasing until at least 2028, vendors are adapting their portfolios to a permanently higher cost structure. The 173 million smartphones below $100, which shipped last year, are facing an existential crisis. Android players focused on low-end devices, which were already operating on razor-thin margins, are cutting low-end models and pushing a higher-end product mix. In Q2 2026, this segment saw an almost 60% YoY drop and is expected to fall faster in the second half…

…The premium end will remain more resilient to the price hikes as long-term interest-free financing options are more prevalent in developed markets like the US and UK. The mass market does not hold up, especially in emerging markets, which are expected to drop over 20% this year. This is why the unit decline continues to deepen while the value line keeps rising.

The report goes on to put it bluntly:

The next 18 months will separate the vendors who can operate in a structurally more expensive market from those who cannot. Apple, Samsung, and Huawei have the scale and pricing power to turn this challenge to their advantage. Smaller Android brands anchored in the entry tiers face the hardest stretch in the industry’s history, and some will not clear it. The market that emerges on the other side of the crisis, when the memory supply finally stabilizes in 2028, will be smaller in units, larger in value, and far more concentrated at the top. The cheap smartphone era is not pausing. It is over.

	

Oof.

The only bright spot is foldables, which are forecasted to grow by 12.6% in 2026 (22.9 million units) and continue accelerating in 2027 to around 27 million units. That’s largely thanks to Apple joining the ranks, though, with its upcoming foldable that’s expected to be announced in just a couple of weeks.

If you thought the Pixel price hikes were bad, it sounds like that’s merely the beginning.

title: If space data centers feel far-fetched, why not interstellar travel?
snippet: The team behind Starcloud's orbital data centers has a new high-risk space project: Sending a probe to Alpha Centauri.
fullText:
The founders behind Starcloud, a startup with plans to operate a fleet of GPUs in orbit, have a new pitch for potential investors: A plan to send a tiny spacecraft on an 80,000 year journey to Alpha Centauri.

If they do it, it will be the first human-built object explicitly aimed for another star, and the sixth to leave our solar system.

Dubbed Fermi Explorer, the non-profit behind the mission emerged today to ask for partners, donations and advice. The initial team—Starcloud founders Philip Johnston, Adi Oltean, and Ezra Feilden, along with program manager Garret Jameson—has put together a plan to use proven space technologies to send a vehicle with a 10 cm square payload, weighing 1 kilogram, into interstellar space. 

The founders say they are launching this mission in the spirit of human exploration; to achieve a historical first; and to test the limits of the Fermi paradox, which attempts to explain why we have yet to find other intelligent life in the universe, and gives the mission its name. 

The mission is intended to cost about $15 million, and to launch in 2029. The non-profit is soliciting vendors to build the vehicle, funding to pay them, and scientific and artistic payloads to send, ala the sensors and Golden Record onboard NASA’s Voyager space probe, the first human spacecraft to leave our solar system. 

Most plans for interstellar exploration stumble when dealing with the vast distances involved and the comparatively slow methods we have to cross them. Voyager, launched in 1977, is now about 26 billion km from Earth; Alpha Centauri, the nearest star to our solar system, is 41 trillion km away.

The last time Silicon Valley took on this challenge, a nonprofit called Breakthrough Starshot, founded in 2016 by Yuri Milner and backed by Mark Zuckerberg, envisioned a multi-billion dollar effort to use a novel laser-based propulsion system to reach Alpha Centauri in twenty to thirty years. The effort collapsed in 2025, but the dream apparently remains alive. 

Fermi Explorer takes the opposite tack: Rather than pushing the frontier of technology, the goal is to use what we have already to do something.

“I also got excited and then disappointed!” Johnston said of Starshot. “That’s the reason we are doing the mission. We are hell-bent on actually launching something in three years. … the big difference with most other [interstellar] missions and the Fermi Explorer is that the others all try to do it in a human lifetime, which means billion-dollar propulsion R&D programs. We have very deliberately picked 80,000 years as the minimum viable mission.”

The plan is to launch the spacecraft on a rocket rideshare, then use efficient but low-power electric propulsion to slingshot the vehicle into a series of orbits that will eventually leave it bound for Alpha Centauri. The spacecraft is intended to be active for about 12 years before entering a final coast phase toward the other solar system.

“If a dinosaur bone can last 200 million years then a metal box can easily survive the radiation environment we expect for 50,000 years,” Johnston said. “We don’t plan on powering spacecraft up at the end of the 80,000 years. We hope that a future human civilization will intercept it.”

title: Apple will be launching its first pair of smart glasses next year: Here’s what’s coming
snippet: As soon as next year, Apple will be debuting its first pair of AI-powered smart glasses. They’ll integrate Visual Intelligence and bring Siri to the real world. Here’s what we’re expecting. more…
fullText:
As soon as next year, Apple will be debuting its first pair of AI-powered smart glasses. They’ll integrate Visual Intelligence and bring Siri to the real world. Here’s what we’re expecting.

Core features

First and foremost, these glasses are AI glasses, not AR glasses. That means they’ll primarily be voice and camera-based, as they won’t have any displays.

The cameras will allow Siri to look at your real world environment and answer questions, provide context, and translate signage. Another feature that we’ll likely see on these glasses is the ability for you to ask Siri to save an image of something and remind you later, as we first saw in the macOS 26.7 leak.

They’ll also offer speakers for music and audio playback, so you can think of them as open-ear headphones.

On the other hand, though – they might not allow for the glasses to take photos and videos normally, per Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman. Meta’s Ray-Ban glasses have become a massive privacy concern lately, and Apple may want to avoid that.

Styles

Unlike Meta, Apple isn’t partnering with an existing eyewear-maker to design these glasses. According to Bloomberg, the company is instead designing them in house, with a number of different styles in the works:

A large rectangular frame, reminiscent of Ray-Ban Wayfarers

A slimmer rectangular design, similar to the glasses worn by Apple Chief Executive Officer Tim Cook

Larger oval or circular frames

A smaller, more refined oval or circular option

They’re supposedly going to be made of acetate, a more durable and higher-end alternative to plastic. Apple will also offer them in a few finishes, including black, ocean blue, and light brown.

Health

In a future iteration of the product, Apple is reportedly considering positioning the product as a health device. This could mean they’ll integrate heart-rate monitors (similar to AirPods Pro 3), and it could mean there’ll be additional software features (like Workout Buddy from Apple Watch) to make it more helpful.

Beyond that, it’s unclear how Apple will make these useful for health – just don’t expect it in the first iteration.

Release date

	

Recent reporting suggests that Apple will unveil these glasses at WWDC 2027 to allow developers to prepare for them. Then, they’ll ship later that year. In all likelihood that’ll mean a September debut, alongside the 20th anniversary all-glass iPhone. You can learn more about that here.

Are you excited for Apple’s first pair of smart glasses? Let us know in the comments.

title: Google Rolls Out 3 New Ways to Book Travel Using AI Mode in Search
snippet: Just in time for Labor Day weekend, Google launches upgraded travel features to book flights, hotels and more.
fullText:
This year has been one of the most jam-packed travel schedules I’ve ever had. Between work conferences and trips with friends, 2026 has felt a bit like Christopher Nolan’s The Odyssey. 

Maybe that’s dramatic, but I’m not the only one jetsetting and roadtripping. 

Millions of Americans are gearing up to travel for Labor Day weekend. While AAA has not yet released its 2026 predictions for total travelers, it has already reported that this Labor Day will see heavier traffic and higher costs. 

Right in time, Google is rolling out three new travel features for AI Mode in Search to book and save. From flight price tracking to hotel booking to understanding your points and miles, here’s what you need to know about these new features to make the most of upcoming travel. 

Google’s new travel features

While I’ve covered numerous Google travel-related rollouts, such as using AI Mode to find items you forgot to pack and planning trips with Gemini and Google Maps, these new features are coming directly to AI Mode in Search. 

First, Google is putting its airfare tracker right in AI Mode. As you chat, you can describe when and where you’re looking to fly to, and you’ll receive a list of the best options available. From there, you can prompt the AI to track airfare for that location on those days or times and set up email notifications if the price changes. 

You’ll also be able to do a similar search and book routine for hotels. You can use AI Mode to research hotel options based on your location, dates and preferences, making comparisons easier. If you’re ready to book, you can now do so right in AI Mode, including booking through Booking.com, Choice Hotels, Expedia, Hilton, Hotels.com, IHG, Marriott, Priceline, Trip.com and Wyndham directly through Google’s AI Mode in Search. 

This feature is available now in the US in English, with plans to expand globally soon. 

Even travel savants struggle to understand how best to use points and miles. Now you can view the cost of airfare and hotels with points or miles added. 

Using AI Mode in Search, you can write something like “I want to fly from Seattle to Boston using AA miles. Help me find nonstop flights in late September” to see what your flights would cost using those miles. 

This feature supports multiple airlines’ rewards systems, including Alaska Airlines/Hawaiian Airlines, American Airlines, Choice Hotels International, Hilton and Wyndham Hotels & Resorts, with plans to add more soon.

title: Clipto uses AI to search terabytes of video and is now valued at $250M
snippet: The three-year-old startup says it reached $15 million in ARR and profitability before raising its latest $15 million round.
fullText:
Generative AI is making it easier to produce more content and harder to keep track of it. As videos, recordings, and documents accumulate, Adobe, Apple, Google, and a growing number of startups are using AI to make those files searchable. It is not yet clear whether that will support a new category of stand-alone software or become a standard feature of products people already use.

Clipto is betting there is room for a separate product. The San Francisco-headquartered startup, which also has teams in Singapore and Hong Kong, has raised $15 million in an all-equity round at a $250 million post-money valuation. The investors include HSG (formerly Sequoia China), GL Ventures, EnvisionX Capital, Palm Drive Capital, Hans Tung, Lu Zhang, and 522 Ventures.

Clipto indexes videos, audio, images, meetings, and other files on a user’s computer. Instead of scrolling through folders to find what you need, users can search by describing what they’re looking for or ask ChatGPT, Claude, or other AI tools to find it for them.

Clipto founder Henry Kang has been working on related problems for roughly two decades. Kang said that, while a PhD student at Carnegie Mellon University in 2006, he worked on robots that recorded their surroundings, identified objects, and remembered where to find them. Kang later applied the same basic idea to his first startup, which used AI to keep track of the clothes in a user’s closet and suggest outfits. His second company, Zenvideo, focused on making video creation easier and was acquired by Tencent in 2020, Kang told TechCrunch.

“The real insight is that in this AI era, we don’t have a content shortage,” Kang said. “The opposite is true. We have too much content. We have too much video footage sitting on our computers that isn’t being used.”

Kang founded Clipto in 2023 with several members of his previous startup’s founding team, building the company around that observation. While other AI companies focused on generating new material, Clipto set out to help users find and reuse files they already had.

Clipto initially built its product for video creators trying to manage footage scattered across computers and external drives. But Kang said creators now make up only about one-quarter to one-third of its users. The rest include lawyers, doctors, researchers, marketers, human-resources professionals, professors and students.

The company says more than 30 million people have used its products since launch and that it has hundreds of thousands of paying subscribers. Kang declined to provide a more precise subscriber count or average revenue per customer, though he said a significant portion of customers remain subscribed for more than two years.

Clipto reached $15 million in annual recurring revenue at the beginning of 2026, and remains profitable on a net-income basis, Kang said. The company has just over 20 employees split among the San Francisco Bay Area, Hong Kong, and Singapore.

About two weeks ago, Clipto added support for Model Context Protocol, or MCP, a standard that allows AI applications to connect with outside sources of information. Kang said access to indexed files requires the user’s active request and authorization. When an AI application accesses Clipto’s indexed data, it can only retrieve information within the scope the user specifies. All of this processing runs locally on the user’s device without requiring cloud services, Kang added.

Clipto is entering a market where larger companies already control much of the data and software people use to manage it. Adobe already offers AI-powered search in Premiere, while Apple Photos and Google Photos allow users to find photos and videos using natural-language descriptions.

Kang said Clipto can search across videos, audio, images, and documents, while products from Adobe, Apple, and Google generally focus on files stored within their own services. Clipto also lets users make selected information available to AI tools such as ChatGPT and Claude. The company is betting that combining those functions in one product will help it compete with larger platforms.

The new funding will go toward the AI models and computing infrastructure needed to run Clipto on consumer hardware, as well as integrations with more AI agents, Kang said.

title: The Year of the Claw: OpenClaw Rolls Out New Version of Its Viral AI Agent
snippet: The agentic AI platform is molting again.
fullText:
Earlier this year, I went on record saying that 2026 would be the year of the AI agent. With the seemingly never-ending rollout of agentic AI since then, I feel validated in that prediction. However, I may make one amendment to that statement now: It’s the year of the claw. 

I first realized agents would be the next big thing in AI when OpenClaw, an open-source AI agent that runs right on your devices and can do a slew of tasks independently on your behalf, went absolutely viral in January. The creator, Peter Steinberger, even joined OpenAI in February to “work on bringing agents to everyone.” 

Now, OpenClaw is regenerating into a newer, more capable lobster. 

OpenClaw recently announced the rollout of OpenClaw 2.0, the “largest update” in its history, bringing a number of fixes, new features and capabilities. Steinberger once said, “Molting is what lobsters do to grow.” And it seems like OpenClaw is shedding its shell and molting to be bigger and better than before. 

What is OpenClaw?

OpenClaw is an AI assistant that doesn’t just chat, but executes tasks on your behalf without any oversight. It can be integrated with the apps you use most often, like WhatsApp, Telegram, iMessage, Slack, Discord, Signal and more, to operate like a personal assistant that never stops to eat, sleep or be human. It also doesn’t need specific hardware to run, making it accessible on really any device you have. 

The assistant went viral across social media, Reddit and internet spaces that are all about AI. Part of the allure was that OpenClaw is open-source, meaning it’s freely accessible for you to use, personalize and share, but also because of its chaotic origin story. 

I already wrote in-depth about the hectic beginnings of OpenClaw, which included multiple renames from Clawdbot to Moltbot to OpenClaw, and broke the internet… twice. The real catch is that while OpenClaw was a huge hit for being capable, autonomous and powerful, it came with equally concerning security risks that were scaling just as fast. (You can read my full analysis of OpenClaw to learn about these security concerns.)

The biggest worry about AI agents is their proclivity to go rogue. These agents will often work to accomplish tasks by any means necessary, even going beyond the settings and boundaries set by the humans who created them. This means they can access the entire internet with minimal effort, prompting experts to call AI agents “cybersecurity nightmares.” 

Despite warnings from cybersecurity experts, OpenClaw has been a global success, even sparking numerous copycats. Many AI companies have spent the better part of a year trying to replicate OpenClaw’s success with the rollout of Gemini Spark, Claude Cowork, ChatGPT Work, Grok Bot and Copilot Studio.      

What is new in OpenClaw 2.0?

OpenClaw 2.0 emerged from the goal of “simpler setup and a first-class browser experience,” according to a blog post about the launch by the OpenClaw Foundation’s Hannes Rudolph. The 2.0 version includes updates to “every part of OpenClaw” from installation, messaging, memory, skills, the browser, plugins, security and numerous fixes, which combined to create a new, revamped experience.

The first major update to the installation process should make it easier for first-time OpenClaw users to get started. The changes include starting the setup with “what is already on someone’s computer,” like your existing ChatGPT or Claude subscriptions, API keys and local models. From there, configuration was simplified to allow you to get prompting quicker and finalze set up later. 

The other big change comes to the browser app, which was rebuilt to open directly into a conversation with your claw (the name for your personal AI assistant in OpenClaw). 

Many people use OpenClaw because it’s genuinely capable. The AI assistant can easily fit into your most-used tools, such as calendar, notes and email, so it feels more like a part of your daily routine and less like autonomous software. If you want to try OpenClaw for yourself, you can visit openclaw.ai for documentation, installation guides and security checklists. If you do decide to take the chance on OpenClaw, make sure you’re aware of the security risks and the potential for agents to go rogue – and maybe consider using a spare laptop.

title: Google AI Mode adds flight price tracking, hotel booking, & more travel tools
snippet: Google is rolling out a trio of updates that boost AI Mode’s travel capabilities, starting with the ability to get price alerts for flights. more…
fullText:
Google is rolling out a trio of updates that boost AI Mode’s travel capabilities, starting with the ability to get price alerts for flights.

Google Flights price tracking is coming directly into AI Mode. This integration starts with the ability to “describe where and when you want to fly.” You’ll see a list of flights and prices from “more than 300 partner airlines and travel sites.”

If you’re ready to book, you can build your full itinerary in AI Mode and buy your tickets through the airline’s website or your preferred booking platform.

Otherwise, you can follow up with “track these flight prices for me.” AI Mode will have you confirm the route, dates, and filters. Price changes will be delivered via email. Flight price tracking in AI Mode is now rolled out in over 180 countries/territories.

AI Mode can now show the cost of flights and hotels in points or miles. At launch, this feature supports Alaska Airlines / Hawaiian Airlines, American Airlines, Choice Hotels International, Hilton, and Wyndham Hotels & Resorts. Support for Accor, Flying Blue, Hyatt, LATAM Airlines, and Lufthansa Group will be available in the coming weeks.

	

This lets you ask: “I want to travel from Atlanta to Miami using my AA miles. Help me find some options for nonstop flights departing Oct 9 and returning on Oct 12.”

…you’ll see how many miles you need to book matching flights, based on the latest data directly from our partners.

The final travel update for AI Mode is hotel booking. This lets you chat about your preferences to get a list of hotels “complete with guest reviews and key factors to compare.” Once found, “Continue on Google” will appear for supported partners. 

From there, it’s just a few taps to pick your room type, review details like the cancellation policy, and complete the booking securely via Google Pay. When you book hotels through AI Mode, the hotel or booking platform will act as the merchant of record and handle any customer service.

This is rolling out now in the US with support for Booking.com, Choice Hotels International, Expedia, Hilton, Hotels.com, IHG Hotels & Resorts, Marriott International, Priceline, Trip.com, and Wyndham Hotels & Resorts.

fullText:
Nvidia is officially launching DLSS 5 this week, following a divisive announcement in March where we likened the AI upscaling tech to a “real-time generative AI filter for video games” and “motion smoothing for video games, but worse.” DLSS 5 will officially be available on RTX 50-series desktop and laptop GPUs and through GeForce Now cloud gaming, though the only game with the tech so far is NBA 2K27 — which is launching September 3rd at 9PM PT on PC.

When it was announced, Nvidia lauded DLSS 5 as “the company’s most significant breakthrough in computer graphics since the debut of real-time ray tracing in 2018,” and highlighted how the tech uses AI to make games look more realistic by enhancing a game based on its source content. Nvidia also stressed that DLSS 5 gave developers controls that let them decide how changes from DLSS 5 appeared in their games.

Image compare: drag the handle to see the difference Nvidia says it can provide in NBA 2K27. Tap here for full-res with DLSS 5 off, and with DLSS 5 on.

But accompanying examples shared by Nvidia were widely criticized and meme’d on for significantly changing how characters looked, such as the “yassification” of Resident Evil Requiem protagonist Grace Ashcroft. With the official launch, Requiem still doesn’t support DLSS 5, and neither do other games shown in the March reveal, including EA Sports FC, Starfield, and Hogwarts Legacy, so we don’t know how the final version of the tech might now appear in those titles.

Nvidia did not answer our questions about when DLSS 5 might come to any game beyond NBA 2K27, nor reconfirm that previously confirmed titles will still include the tech.

In examples from NBA 2K27 we saw in a press briefing, though, changes from DLSS 5 don’t appear to be quite as dramatic as the types of adjustments shown in the initial reveal. The shadows and textures added by DLSS 5 generally made the players in the game look more realistic instead of turning them into AI caricatures. You can see more in our deeper dive here.

In briefings, Nvidia showed how developers will have many sliders at their disposal to determine exactly how much DLSS 5 changes things, and that developers can choose to amp up whichever parts of the scene they prefer. They can even leave characters’ faces alone and just enhance silverware or food or foliage, Nvidia says.

Image slider: drag the handle to make bacon look more real by giving it shadows.

While Nvidia’s original DLSS 5 demos required a pair of RTX 5090 gaming graphics cards, the company claims even a single midrange RTX 5060 can manage to play NBA 2K27 at 1080p with ray tracing and DLSS 5 at ultra spec — if you have one of he fastest gaming CPUs and enable 6x frame generation (meaning the game is only producing one “real” frame for every six frames you see).

DLSS 5 is still a huge performance hit. Nvidia estimates it at 50 to 60 percent, and we saw performance cut in half when we tried an unofficial DLSS5 mod in Shadow of the Tomb Raider.

Image: Nvidia

So far, Nvidia has shown us examples that demonstrate the ideal version of what’s possible with DLSS 5 (and promote NBA 2K27). We haven’t yet tested an official build of DLSS 5 ourselves to get an idea of how the tech might look, but we have tried the unofficial version that modders are using to mess with older games like Control and Skyrim. With older games, it seems, a little sprinkle of DLSS 5 goes a long way.

Follow topics and authors from this story to see more like this in your personalized homepage feed and to receive email updates.

Jay Peters

Nvidia is officially launching DLSS 5 this week, following a divisive announcement in March where we likened the AI upscaling tech to a “real-time generative AI filter for video games” and “motion smoothing for video games, but worse.” DLSS 5 will officially be available on RTX 50-series desktop and laptop GPUs and through GeForce Now cloud gaming, though the only game with the tech so far is NBA 2K27 — which is launching September 3rd at 9PM PT on PC.

When it was announced, Nvidia lauded DLSS 5 as “the company’s most significant breakthrough in computer graphics since the debut of real-time ray tracing in 2018,” and highlighted how the tech uses AI to make games look more realistic by enhancing a game based on its source content. Nvidia also stressed that DLSS 5 gave developers controls that let them decide how changes from DLSS 5 appeared in their games.

title: Here’s how Apple Watch Ultra 4 will differentiate itself from prior models
snippet: Apple Watch Ultra 4 is coming on September 9, here are the key ways it’s rumored to differentiate itself from prior models. more…
fullText:
Apple Watch Ultra 4 is coming on September 9, here are the key ways it’s rumored to differentiate itself from prior models.

‘Significant upgrade’ to health sensors

Digitimes has reported on multiple occasions that Apple Watch Ultra 4 will bring significant upgrades to internal sensors. It went as far as saying “the number of sensor components will double.”

Mark Gurman reported this week that “upgrades to fitness tracking” are coming. And there’s evidence that a new high blood pressure-related feature has been reviewed by the FDA for release soon.

Though many specific details around these sensor additions are still unknown, it sounds like Apple Watch Ultra 4 could lean more than ever into health and fitness tracking.

New S-class chip, the first built in AI era

Last year’s Apple Watch models used the same S10 chip that first debuted in 2024. But the last time the Watch got a truly meaningful speed and performance bump was 2023.

Rumors indicate Apple Watch Ultra 4 and Series 12 will have a brand new, more powerful chip—likely dubbed S11 or S12.

The timing lines up perfectly with Siri AI’s debut in watchOS 27. And no doubt, the first CPU boost in an S-class chip since 2023 will pack improvements that benefit AI features.

There’s a lot of potential for Apple Watch to be the first mass-market AI wearable. I’m excited to see how the new chip might help move that needle.

Wildcard: Design updates

	

There are conflicting reports concerning Apple Watch Ultra 4’s design. While Digitimes claims a redesign is coming, Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman said last month: “None of this year’s watches is expected to get a major design overhaul.”

We do know that a ceramic case option is expected for Apple Watch Series 12. So it’s possible that Apple will similarly offer something unique for Apple Watch Ultra 4’s design. Reporting is unclear, but perhaps we’ll see design updates that differentiate the latest Ultra model.

fullText:
Apple has announced an expansion of its Supplier Employee Development Fund, a $50 million educational program for workers in its supply chain, in the form of a new Apple Education Center in Vietnam.

The country is becoming an increasingly important manufacturing center as Apple diversifies beyond China, and the center operates in partnership with Hanoi University of Science and Technology (HUST) …

Apple first launched its Supplier Employee Development Fund back in 2022 in response to concerns about the welfare of workers in the company’s supply chain. The company committed £50 million and said that it would be geared to a mix of worker education and respect for worker rights.

It will expand access to learning opportunities and skills development. The fund also includes new and expanded partnerships with leading rights advocates, universities, and nonprofits to drive Apple’s ongoing work to empower supplier employees and drive improvements in knowledge of and respect for workplace rights across industries.

The fund’s prior work in the country focused on providing training opportunities for people with disabilities, while this latest development appears to mirror an approach rolled out in India earlier this year.

Technical programs will equip students with on-demand skills such as basic knowledge of smart manufacturing, robotics and automation technology […] The center also provides comprehensive professional development courses. Students will have access to leadership soft skills programs and line-up training, giving them more capacity to advance in their current role or start a completely new career journey.

Apple says that the program has so far seen 9 million training sessions delivered worldwide, while 108,000 supply chain employees have participated in a separate Swift coding program.

title: Poco F9 Pro and F9 Ultra launch with 185Hz panels, 8 Elite Gen 5 chips, and huge batteries
snippet: Xiaomi sub-brand Poco is officially expanding its flagship smartphone line with the launch of the Poco F9 Pro and Poco F9 Ultra. more…
fullText:
Xiaomi sub-brand Poco is officially expanding its flagship smartphone line with the launch of the Poco F9 Pro and Poco F9 Ultra.

Under the hood, the top-tier Poco F9 Ultra packs Qualcomm’s Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 processor paired with up to 16GB of RAM and 1TB of UFS 4.1 storage. The standard Poco F9 Pro relies on the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 5 V Series (SM8850-1-AB) with up to 12GB of RAM and 512GB of storage. Both handsets incorporate a dedicated 12nm VisionBoost D8 graphics chip to handle AI frame insertion and super-resolution processing.

On the front, both devices feature HyperRGB AMOLED panels with a 185Hz refresh rate and peak brightness up to 4,500 nits. The Poco F9 Pro features a 6.59-inch display with a 2510 x 1156 resolution, while the Poco F9 Ultra expands to a 6.9-inch display with a 2608 x 1200 resolution. Both screens feature 480Hz 10-point touch sampling, 4800Hz instant touch sampling, Gorilla Glass 7i protection, and integrated ultrasonic fingerprint sensors.

Camera hardware sees a major overhaul on both models, starting with a shared 200MP primary sensor with optical image stabilization (OIS) and 4K video recording. The secondary camera configurations branch off from there. 

	

The Poco F9 Pro pairs the main camera with a 50MP floating telephoto lens capable of 2.5x optical zoom and an 8MP ultra-wide sensor. The Poco F9 Ultra steps up to a 50MP periscope telephoto lens with 5x optical zoom alongside a 50MP ultra-wide sensor. Both phones include a 32MP front-facing selfie camera.

Audio performance has been tuned in partnership with Bose. The F9 Pro comes equipped with symmetrical dual stereo speakers, whereas the Poco F9 Ultra introduces a 2.1-channel audio configuration that combines dual stereo speakers with an independent 1620 rear subwoofer.

Power endurance is handled by a 6,330mAh battery on the F9 Pro, while the F9 Ultra houses a, frankly, massive 8,050mAh silicon-carbon battery with a 16% silicon content ratio. Both models share the same charging speeds: 100W wired fast charging, 50W wireless charging, 27W wired reverse charging, and 22.5W wireless reverse charging.

Additional standard hardware specifications include IP68 dust and water resistance, NFC support, and Xiaomi HyperOS 3 running out of the box. Color choices for the F9 Pro include Black, White, and Aurora Green, which features a glow-in-the-dark rear cover. The F9 Ultra is available in Black and Dark Cherry with a glass fiber finish and interactive lighting accents on the rear housing.

Pricing for the Poco F9 Pro starts at $699 for the 12GB/256GB base model (early-bird $649) and reaches $769 for the 12GB/512GB tier (early-bird $699). The Poco F9 Ultra starts at $799 for the 12GB/256GB option (early bird $729), $949 for the 16GB/512GB option (early bird $799), and tops out at $1,199 for the 16GB/1TB option (early bird $1,059). Global availability and localized ordering options are available directly on the official Poco Global page and Xiaomi launch portal.

title: Instagram puts new limits on undisclosed AI profiles
snippet: As frustration over AI influencers has been growing, Instagram is limiting the reach of undisclosed AI profiles.
fullText:
Instagram announced Monday that it’s changing how it labels AI-generated profiles and will start limiting the reach of accounts that feature AI-generated people without saying so.

The platform says it’s renaming its existing “AI creator” label to “AI-generated profile,” which Instagram says should make the disclosure easier to understand. The new label is meant to tell users that the person featured on a profile was generated or substantially created with AI.

Under the new policy, creators who don’t properly label an AI-generated profile could see their reach reduced. Creators who use the new label, on the other hand, won’t be penalized simply for having an AI-generated person as their profile subject.

The label also isn’t meant for every use of AI. Instagram says people who use AI to edit photos, polish captions, create graphics, or make other creative tweaks don’t need to use the AI-generated profile label.

Instagram says the change comes partly in response to users who have stumbled across profiles that looked like they belonged to real people, only to find out later that the person was completely AI-generated.

“As generative AI becomes a bigger part of how people create, we’ve heard that people don’t like seeing a profile that seems human, only to find out later that the person featured is AI-generated,” Instagram wrote. “They want to know when a profile features an AI-generated person.”

Image Credits:Instagram

The timing is notable. Frustration over AI-generated content has been growing as AI influencers become more common across social media platforms. 

For instance, earlier this year, the gay dating app Goose became the subject of a Wired investigation after a network of apparently AI-generated male influencers promoted the app on Instagram. Wired found more than two dozen accounts that appeared to feature AI influencers, some of which reportedly reached out to potential users through direct messages to get them to sign up.

Health and wellness content is another particularly worrying example. The New York Times reported in July it found hundreds of AI-generated doctors, healers, and wellness personalities on social media promoting supplements or making health claims to users. 

The announcement comes after Instagram faced backlash over an AI tool that allowed users to generate images using other people’s likenesses. Users objected to having their public Instagram content used without an explicit opt-in. Meta then removed the feature.

Last week, Meta reached an $18 billion settlement with U.S. states over allegations concerning the effects of Facebook and Instagram on children and teenagers. As part of the agreement, Meta will introduce a default two-hour daily usage limit for teens across Facebook and Instagram, a “Night Mode” block, muted notifications during school hours, and other restrictions.

title: Instagram Says It’s Pulling the Mask Off AI Influencers
snippet: Instagram is requiring fake models to carry an AI-generated profile label to show they’re not human.
fullText:
Effective immediately — at least in theory — Instagram is requiring profiles of fake influencers to carry an “AI-generated profile” badge directly beneath the handle and display name in the account’s main bio header.

In a blog post titled Bringing More Transparency to AI-Generated Profiles on Instagram, the Meta-owned social network said Monday that the goal is for viewers to know they’re seeing an AI-generated profile rather than a human one. Previously, some of these accounts carried an AI creator label, which could easily be mistaken for a human who uses AI to create content.

An AI-generated profile label is also supposed to appear on the AI influencer’s individual Feed posts, Reels and Story overlays. Instagram said that AI profiles that don’t implement the label will have their accounts forcibly demoted, meaning posts would be restricted from being recommended to non-followers until the creator adds the label. Those restrictions would apply to Reels, Explore and in-feed suggestions for other Instagram users.

A representative for Meta told CNET in an email that the ability to label profiles has already been rolled out to everybody, but the process of detecting unlabeled profiles and notifying account owners will happen in the coming weeks.

CNET viewed accounts for about a half dozen popular AI-generated accounts, including Tilly Norwood, Aitana Lopez, Lil Miquela and Imma. As of 11 a.m. PT Monday, none of these carried the “AI-generated profile” label. 

According to Instagram’s blog post, the change was motivated by user feedback requesting that any AI-based identity be clearly labeled. “We’ve heard that people don’t like seeing a profile that seems human, only to find out later that the person featured is AI-generated,” the company wrote. 

CNET

Two years ago, Meta introduced ways to label AI-generated images across its social networks, but it has not introduced rules to demote accounts that post such content. Like other social networks, Instagram is dealing with an influx of AI slop. In July, Instagram rolled back an update that allowed people to create deepfakes of other people’s profiles.

How Instagram’s AI label should work

In its post about AI-generated profiles, Instagram said that accounts that already have an AI creator label will have a chance to review and confirm the change to an AI-generated profile or remove the label entirely if that has changed. Presumably, that could happen if a human took over a profile previously generated by AI.

Instagram said there’s an appeals process if an account owner feels they were mislabeled. A successful appeal would get a profile back in recommendations. 

There are some additional questions about how widespread the labels will be. For now, Instagram said the badge only appears on mobile, not on “computers,” which likely means it won’t show up on desktop versions of Instagram.

In a Help Center post, Instagram says that the AI-generated profile label can help build trust with audiences, increase transparency on Instagram and keep accounts eligible for recommendations.

title: iOS 27 beta 8 now available as Apple tests major Siri AI upgrade
snippet: Apple has released the eighth iOS 27 beta for developer testing. iOS 27 beta 8 continues Apple’s summer beta cycle ahead of a public release in September. We’ll update our devices and share what we discover. Update 5:04 p.m. ET: Now available for public beta testers as well. more…
fullText:
Apple has released the eighth iOS 27 beta for developer testing. iOS 27 beta 8 continues Apple’s summer beta cycle ahead of a public release in September. We’ll update our devices and share what we discover.

Update 5:04 p.m. ET: Now available for public beta testers as well. 

Apple releases eighth iOS 27 developer beta for testing

The eighth developer beta is available now through the Settings app on eligible iPhones. If you’re enrolled in the Apple Developer Program, go to Settings > General > Software Update > Beta Updates and choose the iOS 27 Developer Beta.

Today’s developer beta release will likely become iOS 27 public beta 6. The final version for everyone will arrive in the next few weeks.

iOS 27 is all about Siri AI

iOS 27 is one of Apple’s most AI-focused iPhone updates yet. The headline change is Siri AI, Apple’s rebuilt assistant powered by the next generation of Apple Intelligence and new Apple Foundation Models.

Siri AI brings richer conversations, personal context, broader world knowledge, on-screen awareness, and deeper app actions across the system.

On iPhone, Siri AI also gets a new visual experience tied to the Dynamic Island, plus a dedicated Siri app for revisiting conversations across devices.

Visual Intelligence joins Siri too, including a new Siri mode in the Camera app and improvements that affect Camera Control on iPhone.

Apple Intelligence is also expanding across apps. iOS 27 adds AI-powered improvements for Photos, Safari, Passwords, Mail, Messages, Phone, Shortcuts, Home, and more. As we covered in our breakdown of Apple’s new Foundation Models, some capabilities run on-device, while others use Private Cloud Compute.

More iOS 27 features and changes

Beyond Siri and Apple Intelligence, iOS 27 includes a variety of iPhone-specific changes. Apple has refined the Liquid Glass design introduced last year, including a new Liquid Glass transparency slider for adjusting the look of system UI.

There are also performance improvements for app launches, Photos loading, Camera launch in Low Power Mode, AirDrop transfers, and Wi-Fi-to-cellular transitions.

Other iPhone changes include Photos keywords and star ratings, customizable slideshows, smoother Camera behavior, continuous sending in Messages, Dual Capture in FaceTime, custom EQ for AirPods, new recovery options, easier Apple Pay card switching, and AI-generated wallpaper creation.

We’re installing iOS 27 beta 8 now and will update with any notable changes. In the meantime, you can catch up on everything new in iOS 27 from Apple’s keynote list.

Spot any changes in today’s release of iOS 27 beta 8? Let us know in the comments below!

title: Apple Might Add a Pencil to Its First Foldable, but Don’t Expect It at Launch
snippet: Steve Jobs said in 2007 that “nobody wants a stylus” for the iPhone. That could change.
fullText:
A folding phone straddles the line between a smartphone and a tablet, but would you dare control it with… a stylus? Apple reportedly considered adding an Apple Pencil as an accessory to the company’s first foldable phone, expected to be unveiled next week. But don’t expect it to join the party when the so-called iPhone Ultra is unveiled at Apple’s “Surprise and Shine” product launch event on Sept. 9.

Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman reported this week, with “zero doubt,” that Apple has “internally prototyped, tested and considered launching an Apple Pencil for the foldable iPhone.” But Gurman also said it’s “unlikely” that the company will include the accessory when it introduces the Ultra.

A representative for Apple did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

Read more: A Folding iPhone at Last? What to Expect From Apple’s Surprise and Shine Fall Event

The Apple Pencil is a digital stylus that is compatible with the iPad Pro, iPad Air and iPad Mini. It charges up when attached magnetically and has pixel-perfect precision, low latency to reduce stylus movement and screen response and tilt sensitivity for shading and other effects.

There has never been a Pencil for any of Apple’s numerous iPhone models. As Steve Jobs said during the launch of the first iPhone in 2007, “Nobody wants a stylus.”

More sharpening to do

Despite the Pencil’s features, there are hiccups to pairing it with the Ultra, Gurman said. If you open up the foldable but don’t want to use the Pencil, what would you do with it? Also, there is the worry that using the stylus could leave marks on the foldable screen, which may be more delicate than that of other iPhones and iPads.

Gurman added that the Ultra’s Pencil, if it does come to fruition, will be “stubbier” than those used with iPads. The Pencil Pro is 6.53 inches long.

The Ultra will be Apple’s first foldable phone, arriving in that sector years behind other phone-makers such as Samsung, Google and Motorola. Although many tech analysts are calling it the Ultra, Apple has not announced that name. The iPhone Fold has been another name floated as a possibility.

Other phones do have styluses, including three picked as among the best by CNET’s sister site ZDNET: the Samsung Galaxy S25 Ultra, Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 6 and Moto G Stylus 5G.

title: The Pentagon now has its own version of ChatGPT and Grok
snippet: Versions of OpenAI's ChatGPT and SpaceXAI's Grok will join Google's Gemini on the Pentagon's central portal for AI tools.
fullText:
The Pentagon has launched versions of OpenAI’s ChatGPT and xAI’s Grok, giving 3 million civilian and military personnel access to generative AI tools that have been tailored to “warfighter needs.”

ChatGPT Mil and Grok for Government — custom versions of the popular consumer generative AI tools — are now part of GenAI.mil, a centralized, secure portal launched last year. 

GenAI.mil, which offered Google Gemini when it first launched, is designed to give Department of Defense employees access to commercial frontier AI models without sending sensitive government data through ordinary consumer channels. In particular, the official military version is exempt from the data collection that is difficult to avoid in consumer tech products.

And according to the Department of Defense, the generative AI portal has proven popular. GenAI.mil has already onboarded more than 1.7 million unique users out of the department’s 3 million personnel, according to the department.

These latest additions are part of the Pentagon’s broader effort to use AI tools to accelerate work and give the Department of Defense an edge without sacrificing security. They also highlight the absence of Anthropic’s Claude model and the Pentagon’s effort to work with other companies following its dispute with the frontier lab. Anthropic was labeled a supply-chain risk by the Trump administration — a designation that it is currently fighting in court — after it refused to give the Pentagon unrestricted use of its AI tools and instead insisted on certain safety guardrails.

ChatGPT Mil, which came out of the company’s OpenAI for Government program, will offer an experience familiar to commercial ChatGPT users. The tool will focus on chat, files, projects, and custom GPTs, according to the Defense Department. The tool will also support document-heavy, routine unclassified work such as administrative tasks, logistics, planning, and policy. Other features will be added over time.

The Pentagon positioned Grok’s capabilities and potential uses in much broader and  more militaristic terms. 

“Starshield AI’s Grok for Government will provide the warfighter with immediate productivity gains, stronger knowledge continuity and more secure and efficient collaboration,” according to the Defense Department’s press release. (SpaceX’s Starshield AI is a secure satellite network that uses the company’s existing Starlink tech.)

The department added that Grok would allow its military “to execute missions faster and with greater precision across numerous operational contexts, ranging from market research analysis for acquisition professionals to supply-chain management for logisticians.”

The Pentagon has struck deals with a number of other tech companies in a bid to boost its AI capabilities, including Amazon Web Services, Microsoft, Nvidia, and Reflection AI.

title: Harvard Law dropout raises $6M for Blue Voice to build a ‘Harvey for police officers’
snippet: Blue Voice is trained on department-specific laws, local ordinances, protocols, and guidelines that general-purpose AI tools can't access on the public internet.
fullText:
David Lawrence was a Harvard Law student when an on-campus shooting involving a police officer sparked intense controversy over police conduct. Realizing that most policing errors occur when officers lack instant access to department rules, Lawrence dropped out to tackle the problem with AI. He teamed up with co-founders Amit Patankar, a Harvard MBA and former Google engineer, and Michael Gropman, a retired Boston police deputy chief, to launch Blue Voice — a Boston-based AI startup that provides real-time policy guidance to officers in the field.

Three years later, Blue Voice is coming out of stealth with $6 million in funding led by SignalFire and Las Olas VC. Officers at 225 county agencies across 25 states now rely on the tool daily to ensure their actions follow department protocol — a platform Lawrence likens to Harvey, the AI tool widely used by lawyers, or OpenEvidence, which is a similar tool for doctors.

“When an officer makes a decision, they do so from memory or best guess, based on thousands of pages of law, policy, municipal ordinances, and state laws that they’ve internalized and keep in their head,” Lawrence told TechCrunch.

Before Blue Voice, an officer who couldn’t recall a specific protocol — like the exact seventh step required at a crime scene — had few good options: Flip through a 15,000-page manual, wake up a supervisor in the middle of the night, or search generic tools like Google or ChatGPT that lack police-specific training. The problem was that traditional methods took too much time, while consumer AI models delivered incorrect answers up to 30% of the time, Lawrence said.

Blue Voice says it solves this issue because it is trained on department-specific laws, local ordinances, protocols, and guidelines that general-purpose AI tools can’t access on the public internet. The platform also gives officers instant access to detailed school maps on their phones during active-shooter emergencies.

Today, Blue Voice answers a question every minute. Lawrence says that officers feel confident relying on the tool because it always points them directly to original regulations rather than just generating an answer on its own the way ChatGPT would. Rather than dictating actions, the tool simply provides the laws, leaving the final decision to the officers, who combine it with their own field experience.

Over the last year, says Lawrence, Blue Voice grew its customer base elevenfold because police departments see concrete results, including reduced crime and fewer operational controversies.

Blue Voice recently helped prevent a kidnapping after a rookie officer spotted a man pressuring a young girl to enter his vehicle, according to Lawrence. Unsure whether he had legal grounds to intervene, the officer consulted Blue Voice on his phone. The app instantly confirmed that the situation met the legal criteria for “child enticement” — an offense covering attempts to lure a minor for the purpose of committing a crime against them — giving him the immediate authority to act.

In another instance, Blue Voice reminded a department chief that he couldn’t return an officer to active-duty following a shooting without first obtaining a third-party mental health evaluation.

The startup, which competes with PE-backed Lexipol, also recently developed functionality to help detectives solve cold cases.

At a time when police use of AI — such as Flock Safety’s license plate surveillance systems — draws growing criticism, Lawrence hopes Blue Voice proves that properly deployed AI can deliver public safety benefits without sacrificing civil rights.

Lawrence, who previously worked for Connecticut governor Ned Lamont, developed a deep passion for public service and says he has no regrets about leaving law school behind. “This is the best thing I could do with my career and the most impact I could potentially make,” he said.

Graphic performance improvements

The headline feature of Parallels Desktop 27 is a new Metal-based graphics driver that delivers hardware-accelerated OpenGL 4.3 support to Windows virtual machines on Apple silicon, something Parallels says is unique among Mac virtualization tools right now. OpenGL 4.3 is the minimum graphics level required by many professional Windows apps. ArcGIS Pro, ZWCAD, and Blender 4.3 can now run in a virtualized environment on macOS thanks to this enhancement.

Parallels claims up to 160% faster OpenGL graphics performance on M3 and newer Macs. While boasting up to 35% faster 3D rendering in ArcGIS Pro, which cuts overall workflow time by up to 24%.

Better OpenGL support doesn’t just help professional engineering software. It helps anything that leans on that graphics stack, including games. I’m gaming on a PC for the first time in 20 years right now, all of it in a Windows VM on my M5 Pro, and it’s been incredible as I’ve been testing Parallels Desktop 27.

Local AI development gets faster

Parallels Desktop 27 also adds support for Scalable Matrix Extension (SME2) instructions in Linux and Windows VMs on M4 and newer Macs. Parallels notes that this translates to up to 7x faster AI and machine learning matrix operations and up to 1.75x faster neural network inference, with better performance for tools like Ollama and llama.cpp running inside a VM.  Parallels Desktop for Enterprise now lets you use the CLI to determine whether a copy was activated with a license key or SSO, enabling organizations on Jamf to build extension attributes based on that for device management and reporting.

There’s a lot to like in Parallels Desktop 27 for everyone, depending on whether you are an engineer, developer, or gamer. title: Dyson Blasts Into Dental Care With a $499 Camera-Equipped Toothbrush
snippet: Dyson’s entry into dental care makes your standard toothbrush look like a caveman’s toothbrush.
fullText:
Taking care of our teeth is a straightforward process: brush, floss, rinse, done. But with its new CameraJet toothbrush, launched on Tuesday, Dyson wants to simplify the process. The toothbursh has an AI-powered camera that detects gaps between teeth so it can floss while you brush. 

“Our research has shown that people consistently miss the areas where plaque forms: the gaps between teeth,” Founder and Chief Engineer James Dyson said in a press release. “We wanted to solve three fundamental problems: how to see those gaps, remove plaque and how to improve cleaning performance while brushing.”

The Dyson CameraJet was developed by 661 Dyson engineers and 30 dental professionals over six years.Dyson

A camera for capturing your pearly whites

The toothbrush’s camera uses a 100,000-pixel macro lens with a light. It’s powered by the company’s trademarked AI machine-learning algorithm, Gap Optical Targeting, which was trained on 470,000 dental images collected by Dyson during development.

Gap Optical Targeting analyzes 28 live images per second to detect gaps between teeth within 100 milliseconds. The CameraJet’s jet then shoots a burst of mouthrinse at the gap to floss it. 

Since the CameraJet also connects to 2.4-GHz Wi-Fi and Bluetooth, you can use the camera as an endoscope to see a live view in the brush’s live-viewing or auto-jetting modes. In the app, you can also see coverage maps, guided cleaning, brushing and flossing insights and feedback. 

According to the press release, no images are recorded or stored on the product or in the cloud. All images remain private to the CameraJet user.

	

			

	

			

									

						Dyson CameraJet					

							

		

How the CameraJet’s jet differs

In collaboration with the National University of Singapore’s Faculty of Dentistry for over five years, Dyson created its own proxy plaque to test its flossing jet. Researchers found that traditional water flossers tend to use a needle-like jet that pierces a hole in plaque but doesn’t remove it entirely.

In contrast, the CameraJet uses a conical jet that provides wider coverage while operating at a lower pressure to remain gentle. 

You’ve got a camera, light and mouthrinse jet all in one toothbrush.Dyson

Built with an anti-gravity tank

To contain the recommended amount of mouthrinse for its jet, the CameraJet has a built-in 12.5-ml tank that delivers mouthrinse in any orientation. 

Unlike other water flossers that use what Dyson described in its press release as a “straw in a cup” design, this anti-gravity tank was designed to minimize air pockets that could prevent the jet from firing, especially when the device is horizontal while cleaning the back of the teeth.

Baroque brush heads

Every dual-bristle brush head comes with its own RFID (radio-frequency identification) tag that allows the CameraJet to detect when a brush head is connected and how many times it has been used. This helps users know when it’s time to replace the brush head with a fresh one. 

For less noise, each brush head was also created with a sonic dampener. 

To keep the bristles in constant motion and prevent stalling, the CameraJet uses variable sonic oscillation, which varies the oscillation angle as you brush. This is particularly useful in areas of your mouth that are tough to access, as external lab testing found that the CameraJet’s variable mode removes up to 69% more plaque than market-leading premium electric toothbrushes in hard-to-reach areas. 

On the toothbrush, you can choose between auto-detect and manual jetting modes, and adjust the brushing intensity. 

For sensitive teeth and gums, a sensitive-bristled brush head is also available. 

Below the power button, you can switch between auto-detect and manual jetting modes and change the brushing intensity. Dyson

The price is on the higher side 

Now available on the Dyson website in ceramic ultra blue and ceramic pink, the $499 CameraJet comes with two regular brush heads, a charging dock, a charging cable and a travel case.

In addition to charging the toothbrush, the dock can also refill its mouthrinse tank in three seconds. 

It’s recommended that you use a clear, SLS-free mouth rinse and an SLS-free toothpaste with the CameraJet to prevent foam from interfering with the camera. SLS is a common foaming agent in toothpaste, shampoo and soaps.

However, if you’re looking for a smart toothbrush with a cleaning coach that’s under $499, CNET recommends the $100 Oral-B iO Series 5 on our list of the best electric toothbrushes.

The charging station refills the CameraJet with mouthrinse in three seconds.Dyson

Coming soon

Dyson developed a proprietary non-foaming toothpaste without SLS and a low-foaming mouthrinse specifically designed for the CameraJet’s jet. While no specific release date is available, Dyson said both are coming soon. 

The CameraJet is currently on its way to my home for testing, so I’ll post a review once I find out if it’s worth the price.

title: Brave’s Browser Hides Your Real Email When You’re Signing Up for Websites
snippet: The company launched the email aliases feature, which forwards messages from a dummy address to your main email account.
fullText:
Have you ever received the dreadful notification that your go-to email address was exposed during a data breach? Me, too — but one browser touting itself as an alternative to Google Chrome just might have the solution.

Brave announced last Thursday that it has launched a new “email aliases” feature for its browser, allowing you to create several managed dummy email addresses that contain no personal information and will forward all relevant mail to your main email account.

There are multiple problems with sharing your email during a website sign-up. Aside from the obvious threat of bad actors trying to scrape your sensitive information during a data leak or the nuisance of your main account being targeted by repeated phishing scams, your email address can be used to track you across the web.

According to Brave, “ad tech companies like Google, Meta and LinkedIn publicly promote how businesses can upload email addresses to match customers against their own user profiles.” These companies have been known to trade information to find out what you buy and where you buy it, and continue to accumulate information about you. Brave writes that its email aliases were built to “plug this privacy hole.”

How to use Brave’s email aliases feature

The new email aliases feature isn’t automatically turned on, even if you’re already using Brave’s browser. There are a few easy steps you can follow to sign up for a free Brave account, start generating your five free dummy addresses and find your forwarded mail.

Navigate to the Brave login page (located at brave://settings/email-aliases) during your Brave desktop browsing session.

Sign up and verify your main email address.

While using the Brave browser, right-click on any website’s email address field in order to create and use a new email alias.

To manage email aliases, navigate to the “autofill & passwords” page located within the Brave browser settings.

All email alias mail will be forwarded to the email address used to sign up for the Brave account. Check the spam folder frequently to ensure no mail falls through the cracks.

But wait, doesn’t that mean Brave has my main email address?

Yes, you need to use your main email address to sign up for Brave (the company needs that address to forward you your mail). But having your main email in one place is better than having it spread all over the internet, caught up in hacks and potentially sold to data brokers.

Brave has also made several security assurances that make it seem less likely that your sensitive information is in jeopardy when using the email aliases service.

According to Brave’s blog post, all data associated with the alias emails is encrypted at rest, meaning it’s cryptographically scrambled up for the little time it remains on the company’s servers.

“Brave doesn’t read the contents of emails sent to an alias,” the post reads. “We only process emails to perform standard spam and virus filtering (we need to do this to maintain our status as a reputable email provider). Once an email is delivered, it is deleted from our servers within seconds.”

Brave also promises that any notes you might add to your email aliases are stored locally on your computer, and not on Brave servers. If you use Brave’s online syncing service, the company promises those notes “will be encrypted end-to-end between devices on the same sync chain.”

The new feature is available for free, but you’re currently limited to five aliases. For most people, this will be more than enough to prevent dropping your main email address anywhere on the web — but Brave plans to add more email alias features to its Premium plan in the future.

Representatives for Brave and Google did not immediately respond to a request for comment.

title: Microsoft tests fix for latest hours-long Outlook outage
snippet: Microsoft says it's testing a fix for the widespread Outlook issues that have led to email delays and failures.
fullText:
In Brief

Posted:

11:56 AM PDT · August 31, 2026

Image Credits:Jaap Arriens/NurPhoto / Getty Images

		

							

											
									

					

	

Snow day? Microsoft on Monday confirmed a widespread, multi-hour outage affecting Outlook users, leading to email delays and failures, authentication issues, and other problems.

In a post on X, Microsoft reported the issue was impacting its Exchange Online service, its cloud-hosted platform for business email, calendar, contacts, and tasks, and then said it had identified the problem.

“We’ve confirmed that users may experience degraded functionality with various Exchange Online functionalities. We’re reviewing service telemetry and diagnostic data to isolate the source of the issue,” Microsoft wrote at 12:43 p.m. ET on Monday, after an earlier message saying it was investigating user reports of Exchange Online problems.

The company said that it identified an issue with an “authentication component” and is testing what it believes will be a remediation strategy with a portion of the infrastructure to determine if it resolves the problem. If so, it will roll out the solution more broadly. Later, it noted that the authentication component was impacting other services beyond Exchange.

We've identified an issue with an authentication component which is contributing to impact. To address this, we've developed a remediation strategy and we're applying it to a portion of infrastructure to test its efficacy. Once we've confirmed this resolves impact, we'll apply…

— Microsoft 365 Status (@MSFT365Status) August 31, 2026

We're continuing to fine-tune our remediation strategy as our internal tests progress. Additionally, we've confirmed that the authentication component issue impacts other services beyond Exchange Online. For more information regarding other impact scenarios, please see:…

— Microsoft 365 Status (@MSFT365Status) August 31, 2026

The outage is another reminder of how much of the business world today still runs on email, and particularly Outlook and Exchange.

This has been a fairly lengthy outage, as user reports started streaming in around 11:30 a.m. ET on Monday, according to the crowdsourced outage detection website Downdetector. By 2 p.m. ET, the site was seeing north of 5,000 user reports. Meanwhile, many others were complaining directly on social media platforms, like X.

Those impacted by the outage may see delays and failures in sending or receiving messages, failures when trying to search for content in their mailbox, authentication errors, failures with mailbox operations, and other workflows related to message delivery.

As of 5 PM ET on Monday, Microsoft was still trying to resolve the problem.

title: Galaxy S26 Ultra is the world’s most popular Android phone, and that’s a first
snippet: Android phones are never the top-selling smartphones globally, but the ones that get closest are almost always budget models. In Q2 2026, though, Samsung achieved a major win with the Galaxy S26 Ultra topping the charts as the best-selling Android phone globally. more…
fullText:
Android phones are never the top-selling smartphones globally, but the ones that get closest are almost always budget models. In Q2 2026, though, Samsung achieved a major win with the Galaxy 

S26 Ultra topping the charts as the best-selling Android phone globally.

Counterpoint Research details the top 10 best-selling smartphones globally in Q2 2026 with, shocker, three iPhones at the top. The base iPhone 17 topped the charts, followed by a duo of iPhone 17 Pro models. It’s basically identical to the same time in 2025, but with a key difference – they’re followed up by the Galaxy S26 Ultra instead of a budget device.

Where the Galaxy S25 Ultra barely broke into the top 10 last year, Samsung’s latest flagship beat out the budget-focused Galaxy A07 and A17 for that #4 spot. 

The Galaxy S26 series launched in late February, but the Ultra didn’t make it into Q1’s best-seller list, showing that a huge portion of Samsung’s sales came after the initial launch. Counterpoint explains:

	

The Samsung Galaxy S26 Ultra was the best-selling Android smartphone, marking the first time an ultra-premium Android device has led Android sales in a June quarter. Meanwhile, the later launch of the Galaxy S26 series compared with the Galaxy S25 series shifted more sales into Q2, the Galaxy S26 Ultra outperformed its predecessor and accounted for more than half of the series’ sales. Industry-first privacy display along with enhanced AI capabilities differentiate the smartphone from its peers. Samsung has further increased its focus on flagship smartphones, boosting promotions and strategically allocating resources to mitigate the revenue decline amid rising costs.

title: Google is making AI Overviews even bigger on some search queries
snippet: As AI continues to be a bigger and bigger part of Google Search, the company is making AI Overviews bigger on some searches. more…
fullText:
As AI continues to be a bigger and bigger part of Google Search, the company is making AI Overviews bigger on some searches.

Already placed above traditional search results, Google’s AI Overviews provide an AI-generated answer to your query, pulling that information from links around the web and placing some of those links within the answer. 

Now, those are getting bigger.

In some search queries, Google will automatically fully expand AI Overviews, effectively turning the whole page into an AI response rather than just taking up the very top of the page. The change was first spotted by Chris Long, and Google has confirmed the update to Search Engine Roundtable, saying:

	

For some queries, AI Overviews may dynamically expand for topics where our systems determine it’s most useful for people. Our research has shown that with this dynamic experience, users find Search more helpful and engage deeper in follow-up exploration.

One example of where this happens consistently is with definitions, where AI Overviews take up the entire screen.

title: Unusual timing of Mac mini and Mac Studio updates all about AI, claims report
snippet: Apple surprised many when it quietly announced updated Mac mini and Mac Studio models shortly before its September event. We would normally have expected these announcements to be part of that event. One strong theory is that the company may be making a lot of big announcements in its ‘Surprise and shine‘ keynote, and therefore wanted to get these updates out of the way beforehand. But a new report presents another theory … more…
fullText:
Apple surprised many when it quietly announced updated Mac mini and Mac Studio models shortly before its September event. We would normally have expected these announcements to be part of that event.

One strong theory is that the company may be making a lot of big announcements in its ‘Surprise and shine‘ keynote, and therefore wanted to get these updates out of the way beforehand. But a new report presents another theory … 

Announcing the new Mac mini and Mac Studio models just a fortnight ahead of the September 9th event seemed surprising. Why not wait the extra couple of weeks and do it properly, rather than just via press releases?

The Information says that the decision was made because the company was taken by surprise by the level of demand for the models for AI applications, and with some configurations unavailable for months, Apple brought the announcements forward for this reason.

9to5Mac’s Take

There’s certainly no doubt that the power of Apple Silicon has made both the Mac mini and Mac Studio popular options for those wanting to run AI models locally. For example, we’ve seen researchers use Thunderbolt 5 to turn four Mac Studios into an extremely powerful AI cluster.

I can also believe that Apple did not initially predict the scale of demand this was going to generate.

What seems less likely, however, is the idea that two weeks makes any worthwhile difference to the situation. To me, it’s just too small a gap for this to be a credible explanation. Personally, I think the existing theory we outlined is the more likely one.

Apple will want to make a very big fuss about the launch of its first foldable iPhone and also ensure that the iPhone 18 Pro isn’t seen as an also-ran. If Apple does indeed unveil the HomePad smart home hub as we expect, that too will be a major announcement.

We then need to add in a new Apple TV and HomePod mini 2 – both with Siri AI capabilities – two new Apple Watch models, and potentially new AirPods too. That’s a lot of announcements for a single keynote, so I could absolutely understand wanting to launch the new Mac desktops beforehand.

What’s your view? Please share your thoughts in the comments.

title: Android 17 boosts network security by hiding domain names, lets carriers disable 2G
snippet: Google is out with a blog post today recapping new network security measures in Android 17. more…
fullText:
Google is out with a blog post today recapping new network security measures in Android 17.

Even with HTTPS connections, the domain names of websites (including apps) are “still visible to network operators and eavesdroppers.” 

This unencrypted data can be used to build user profiles or, in the hands of malicious actors, leveraged for targeted phishing and scam campaigns.

Android 17 aims to resolve this with Encrypted Client Hello (ECH). Working with private DNS, this new privacy standard will “obscure the domain names you visit.” This works by hiding the “domain name using a secret encryption key that only the destination website can unscramble.”

By encrypting the destination website name from the very start, ECH helps ensure that, for supported websites and apps, network providers and network snoopers can no longer easily see which websites or apps you are accessing.

With OS support now available, app developers have to upgrade to OkHttp 5.5.0 and enable ECH.

	

Domain name data leaks in two places, (1) the initial DNS lookup and (2) the unencrypted ClientHello in the Transport Layer Security (TLS) handshake. Recent progress with the rollout of encrypted DNS and the launch of support for Encrypted ClientHello on Android 17 are helping to make online activity more private

On the network front, Android 17 allows mobile carriers to turn off 2G connectivity by default for their users. (Android 12 first introduced this user setting.) This is intended to counter SMS blaster attacks that “force nearby smartphones to drop their LTE or 5G connections and downgrade to less secure, legacy 2G networks.” Phishing texts are then sent to devices.

Meanwhile, Android 17 enforces Local Network Protection wherein apps must now request permission “before they can scan or connect to other devices on your local network.”

For everyday tasks like casting a video to your TV, developers should adopt a secure system tool, which allows you to select your TV without the app ever needing permission to see the other devices in your home.

Finally, Certificate Transparency requires “all certificates to be logged in a public registry, making such an attack much less likely to go unnoticed.”

When you connect to a secure app or website, your device verifies a certificate to confirm the site is authentic. However, if a certificate issuer is compromised, hackers could potentially create fake certificates to intercept your traffic and cause harm.
