title: CarPlay keeps getting better with three recent exciting app updates
snippet: CarPlay is about to get even better with iOS 27 in September. New features including a dedicated Siri app and Siri AI will upgrade Apple’s car infotainment system for iPhone users. Even before the big iPhone software update officially launches, CarPlay in August has improved for everyone with three big app releases. more…
fullText:
CarPlay is about to get even better with iOS 27 in September. New features including a dedicated Siri app and Siri AI will upgrade Apple’s car infotainment system for iPhone users.

Even before the big iPhone software update officially launches, CarPlay in August has improved for everyone with three big app releases.

MLB iPhone app enhances CarPlay experience

First, MLB upgraded their iPhone app in the middle of the baseball season to improve the CarPlay experience.

Fans can browse live and upcoming games, select a matchup, and choose their preferred team’s radio feed. 

CarPlay also now shows baseball scores and key game details while the broadcast plays, with the app’s hide-scores setting respected for anyone avoiding spoilers.

Next, Meta AI for iPhone now works with CarPlay — with a catch.

The Meta AI app joins three other third-party chatbot apps that work with CarPlay: ChatGPT, Perplexity, and Grok.

However, Meta AI on CarPlay appears to be in limited testing for now.

Still, this shows the key benefit of CarPlay: integrating existing iPhone apps with your vehicle. You just can’t expect this amount of AI chatbot choice from built-in infotainment systems.

CarPlay adds a major weather app

The third big CarPlay app in August is Storm Radar from The Weather Channel.

Storm Radar for CarPlay includes a map of your location. You can toggle between satellite view and the default map background. Data layers include radar, clouds, and precipitation. 

Navigation is also a core part of the CarPlay app. Storm Radar displays your current weather conditions alongside the ETA and weather conditions expected at your destination.

The Weather Channel adds that CarPlay support includes “automatic rerouting and weather alerts along your route that refresh as you drive.”

More CarPlay upgrades

Looking ahead, Apple will upgrade CarPlay for everyone with the upcoming iOS 27 iPhone update. Installing the iPhone software update or upgrading to a new iPhone running iOS 27 when it comes out will automatically add new features to CarPlay.

In the meantime, Volvo has upgraded three SUVs with Spatial Audio through CarPlay for Apple Music and Apple Podcasts. This brings Dolby Atmos sound support to drivers. Earlier this year, Pioneer released an aftermarket head unit that similarly drives Dolby Atmos and Spatial Audio through CarPlay.

title: Get ready for a really busy month of smartphones
snippet: At what point are there simply too many phones? | Image: Cath Virginia / The Verge We're not even half a day into September, and two new smartphones have already launched: the Poco F9 Pro and F9 Ultra. We're expecting more this week, as the IFA trade show kicks off in Berlin, before we get new iPhones a week after that. And that's only the beginning of what promises to be an exceptionally busy month for smartphone launches. For the decade I've worked in the industry, tech journalists have always spoken in hushed tones about the dreaded "Techtember," when just about every tech company on the planet seems to be in unspoken agreement that it's time to launch new products in time for the holiday buying season. (It's followed, … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
We’re not even half a day into September, and two new smartphones have already launched: the Poco F9 Pro and F9 Ultra. We’re expecting more this week, as the IFA trade show kicks off in Berlin, before we get new iPhones a week after that. And that’s only the beginning of what promises to be an exceptionally busy month for smartphone launches.

For the decade I’ve worked in the industry, tech journalists have always spoken in hushed tones about the dreaded “Techtember,” when just about every tech company on the planet seems to be in unspoken agreement that it’s time to launch new products in time for the holiday buying season. (It’s followed, in particularly packed years, by Techtober too). In the last few years the pressure has lessened a little, the release calendar stretching out into neighboring months. But in 2026 Techtember is back with a vengeance, especially when it comes to phones.

It always starts with IFA. Europe’s biggest tech trade show attracts over 200,000 visitors and global manufacturers from across tech. IFA doesn’t have as many phone launches as it did a decade ago, when the likes of Sony, Samsung, and LG would routinely launch flagships at the show, but there’s still plenty on the way this week.

Tecno has teased a bezelless concept phone, which it says it’ll be bringing to the show. TCL usually brings an array of E Ink-esque Nxtpaper phones to show, so I’d hope to see some at its press conference. There’s even an outside chance of a whole new foldable: Xiaomi is attending IFA for the first time ever, just a week after it teased the upcoming Xiaomi 18 Fold and promised the phone a launch in early September. Its September 3rd press conference would certainly make sense for that.

Then there’s Apple. The company won’t be at IFA, but it has already announced a September 9th event, where we expect it to launch new iPhones. Rumor has it that it’s splitting its launch up in an act of solidarity with overworked phone reviewers (I wish), delaying the regular iPhone 18 to next spring and sticking to the Pros this month. Still, the long-awaited arrival of the first foldable iPhone should be enough to keep us busy.

But that’s far from all that’s coming. Android Headlines reckons at least 20 phones will launch this month, and that might be a conservative estimate.

Huawei will launch its latest trifold, the Mate XT 2, in China on September 7th, and perhaps the Mate 90 lineup too. Xiaomi will follow up the 18 Fold with the 18 Pro lineup later in the month. Vivo has confirmed its flagship X500 series will also arrive in September, and Honor has done the same for its Magic 9 flagships. Oppo’s Find X10 line has been heavily tipped to arrive in September too, though thankfully some suggest it might slip to the following month. Even OnePlus is expected to get in on the action: its OnePlus 16 rumored to release in September too — though not in the US or Europe.

Why the sudden glut? I blame Qualcomm. It used to launch its flagship Snapdragon chips in December, but that launch date has steadily moved forward, in part to give manufacturers time to ship new products ahead of lucrative holiday sales seasons, both in China and abroad. So this year it’s holding its annual Snapdragon Summit from September 22nd to 24th, when it’s likely to reveal the Snapdragon 8 Elite Gen 6. Promptly after that, we can expect a rush of Android manufacturers announcing phones powered by the new silicon.

With RAMageddon in full swing, the jury’s still out on how appealing these launches will be. Outside of Samsung’s fun Galaxy Z Fold 8, a lot of this year’s biggest phones have been rehashes of 2025 models with a price hike and a chipset bump — and occasionally not even that. At least we’ll have more foldables to be excited about, and hopefully a couple of manufacturers have another surprise or two in store.

A month chock-full of phones, that I can do. But if we’re about to get a Techtember full of iterative updates that cost more, without delivering anything special? Wake me up when it’s Techtober.

title: Apple shares ‘shocking evidence’ against former employee accused of stealing company data for OpenAI
snippet: Apple says it has evidence that a former employee destroyed evidence of data theft after learning he was under investigation.
fullText:
In its lawsuit against OpenAI, Apple filed what it calls “shocking evidence” to bolster its allegations that former employees stole trade secrets for OpenAI’s benefit. These new details emerged after the legal counsel for former Apple employee Chang Liu — who now works at OpenAI — handed over Liu’s old Apple work laptop for investigation earlier this month.

Apple now alleges that Liu used a confidential Apple circuit schematic in his work at OpenAI, as well as a tool that shares a name with an internal Apple engineering application. The company claims that OpenAI was “well-aware” of Liu’s access to Apple data, and that Liu enlisted OpenAI colleague Yu-Ting Peng to help destroy evidence in June when he learned that Apple was investigating him.

“The MacBook represents the very limited information Defendants provided so far (and only after weeks of delay), and shows Apple is not conducting ‘fishing expeditions’ but that its trade secrets are being used and evidence is being destroyed,” the filing reads.

While this new evidence is redacted from public view, past filings from Apple have included text messages from Liu — which he punctuated with “crying laughing” emojis — showing he was aware that he still had access to Apple files.

OpenAI has previously defended Liu by saying that he only accessed Apple files after he stopped working there in order to help former colleagues who asked for his assistance. “Apple now tries to shift the blame to ‘residual access,’ but they also don’t disclose that this is a common issue with Apple which is caused by them failing to properly manage system access when people leave,” OpenAI wrote in a blog post earlier this month. 

But Apple claims that Liu had continued access because he “exploited a rare, previously unknown authentication bug.”

TechCrunch has requested comment from OpenAI on Apple’s newest allegations.

Apple is seeking a preliminary injunction — a court order that would block OpenAI from working on hardware based on Apple’s technology while the case is ongoing — as well as expedited discovery, a fast-tracked process for gathering evidence, since the company alleges that more former employees may also be implicated. 

According to Apple’s initial filing, more than 400 former Apple employees now work at OpenAI.

title: Galaxy S26 gets Fold 8 features in latest Android 17 beta
snippet: Samsung has released a new beta verison of Android 17 for the Galaxy S26, and it’s an exciting one that packs a bunch of the Galaxy Z Fold 8’s features for Samsung’s flagship slab phone. more…
fullText:
Samsung has released a new beta verison of Android 17 for the Galaxy S26, and it’s an exciting one that packs a bunch of the Galaxy Z Fold 8’s features for Samsung’s flagship slab phone.

Since Samsung has been releasing batches of phones by device type, the newest lineup is the Galaxy Z Fold 8, consisting of the smaller, more boxy model and the Galaxy Z Fold 8 Ultra, which is essentially an upgraded version following the previous design language the company put in place.

With that, Samsung released One UI 9 in full. It came with features like Call Brief, customized Now Brief cards, and Fan Cam. The software update also incorporated a new implementation of the Google Search bar on the homescreen. And it’s optional, so it doesn’t need to be there if you prefer it not to.

Samsung is currently rolling those features out to the Galaxy S26, S26 +, and S26 Ultra in its One UI 9 beta program, based on Android 17, in builds S948BXXU4ZZHK, S948BOXM4ZZHK, and 5948BXX14BZHK (via SammyGuru). The changelog lumps the above-mentioned features into one changelog entry. It follows with “improved intermittent device rebooting in specific situations” and “improved usability of ‘Do not disturb’

mode.”

	

One UI 9 beta is still only available for Galaxy S26 devices through the Samsung Members app. Other devices are still in line, like the Galaxy S25 series. But Samsung hasn’t made any comment on its rollout timeline for the One UI 9 beta on older devices.

title: As a relatively new Apple Vision Pro user, this is my favorite way to use it
snippet: Apple Vision Pro is one of Apple’s most interesting hardware releases yet. It’s technically very impressive, yet it seems almost certain that this form factor won’t last – and is instead just a temporary platform to introduce visionOS to the world before we eventually get glasses. I did buy one late last year, and while I haven’t been a major user of it, there is one use case that genuinely makes it enjoyable. more…
fullText:
Apple Vision Pro is one of Apple’s most interesting hardware releases yet. It’s technically very impressive, yet it seems almost certain that this form factor won’t last – and is instead just a temporary platform to introduce visionOS to the world before we eventually get glasses.

I did buy one late last year, and while I haven’t been a major user of it, there is one use case that genuinely makes it enjoyable.

When Vision Pro launched, the potential seemed endless. It’d be the headset to end all screens. Mac Virtual Display seemed awesome, and so did the idea of spatial FaceTime – even if Persona’s were a bit jarring at launch.

Then, once the honeymoon phase wore off, people started to realize the headset was quite heavy, making it hard to use for a long period of time. This meant that a lot of people begun selling their Vision Pros, allowing you to pick up a used one for a substantially discounted price.

They average around $1500 right now – a much smaller pill to swallow than the new $3699 starting price point.

If Vision Pro excels at one thing, it’s content consumption. The App Store might not be the most compelling in most regards, though you do have most streaming apps, including Disney+, HBO Max, and even YouTube now. Netflix is the biggest outlier. Of course, you also have Apple TV.

The best way to enjoy Vision Pro

Outgoing Apple CEO Tim Cook shared his favorite way to use Vision Pro back in January 2025, and recently referenced it again last month in an interview at the season 4 premiere of Ted Lasso:

Funnily enough, Cook was asked if he plans to watch Ted Lasso season 4 on Apple Vision Pro. That was reportedly how he watched season 3. “Oh yes, of course, and watch it lying down on Vision Pro, there’s nothing quite like that.”

I can’t say I exclusively watch shows and movies in Vision Pro. It’s a lot to commit to sometimes, since multitasking on Vision Pro is sometimes a struggle with its poor software keyboard.

When I am watching a show or movie in Vision Pro, though, I am exclusively doing it using the Tim Cook method: lying down and staring upwards. It completely erases the weight concern, and is a pretty relaxing experience if you have the time to commit to it.

Vision Pro is a rather expensive product to only use to occasionally watch television, at least at its MSRP. With how much they’ve depreciated though, I think buying one just to use as a bedtime face TV isn’t necessarily an awful idea. It’s an enjoyable experience, especially when you’re watching in 3D.

title: Apple Card keeps getting better, here’s everything new
snippet: Apple Card launched seven years ago this month, and it keeps getting better. There are new features, perks, rewards, and more. Plus, there’s one major change looming. Here’s everything new with Apple Card lately. more…
fullText:
Apple Card launched seven years ago this month, and it keeps getting better. There are new features, perks, rewards, and more. Plus, there’s one major change looming.

Here’s everything new with Apple Card lately.

iOS 27: Recurring transactions

As my colleague Ryan highlighted last month, iOS 27 adds a really useful new “Recurring” feature to the Wallet app for Apple Card. You can find the “Recurring” hub by tapping the three-dot menu in the top-right corner.

In this menu, you’ll see a list of upcoming recurring transactions that are set to be charged to your Apple Card. This includes the date and the amount of the expected transaction. In addition to viewing the transactions as a list, you can also see them on a monthly calendar view.

It’s a helpful new feature for Apple Card users in iOS 27. The update is currently available to public beta testers and developers, and will likely be released to everyone next month.

New status perk

Earlier this month, Apple added a new perk for Apple Card users who travel a lot.

Apple has teamed up with Booking.com to offer all Apple Card users “Genius Level 2” status after one stay or car rental. You also get 3% Daily Cash on all Booking.com transactions.

What do you get with “Genius Level 2” status? Apple says your status could “unlock benefits on select stays and car rentals such as 10–15% discounts, free breakfast and room upgrades.”

Hertz partnership

Last year, Apple announced a partnership with Hertz to provide exclusive perks when you book a caar rental with your Apple Card:

Free Emergency Roadside Service

Add loss damage waiver vehicle protection for the discounted rate of $16.95 per day (plus tax).

Add a free additional driver at pickup.

Save at least 5% off Pay Later base rates.

Additionally, Apple Card offers 3% Daily Cash for car rentals booked through Hertz.

Apple Card Savings Account expansion

One criticism people have of Apple Card is that it relies on your iPhone for key account management features. Since the Apple Card launch, Apple has worked to improve that.

Most recently, Apple launched web access for Apple Card Savings. This means you can now view and manage your Apple Card Savings Account directly in your web browser.

A big change looms

The big change hanging over Apple Card right now, however, is its impending move from Goldman Sachs to Chase. Apple announced the deal back in January and said the transition will occur “in approximately 24 months.”

Many questions remain about what Apple Card’s future looks like under Chase. Apple has promised that several key things about Apple Card won’t change under Chase’s leadership. We should learn more concrete details over the next 18 months as Chase, Goldman Sachs, and Apple iron out the details behind the scenes.

Wrap up

Are you an Apple Card cardholder? What do you think about it? Personally, I think it’s an excellent option for people in the Apple ecosystem, even if you can usually find better rewards through other ecosystems. I use my Apple Card to pay for my Apple subscriptions to get 3% Daily Cash back. The option to finance Apple hardware purchases with 0% interest is also very compelling.

Let me know what you think down in the comments.

title: Sony Debuts Ad-Supported Live TV on PS5 with Over 100 Channels
snippet: Sony’s ad-supported service includes news, TV, movies, sports and anime.
fullText:
Seven years after Sony closed its paid PlayStation Vue service, the company is debuting free Live TV on PS5 today, with over 100 live channels.

Also read: Best Free TV Streaming Services: Tubi, Roku Channel and More

The ad-supported Live TV will include content from Sony Pictures Television and others, such as NBC and Fox News; sports; movies from MovieSphere and FilmRise Free Movies; TV shows such as The Walking Dead; and anime from Crunchyroll.

To access the service, navigate to the Media tab on the home page and click on the Live TV on PS5 icon. Sony confirmed to CNET that the service will be coming to Bravia TVs later in the year.

The service will also include “gaming and esports content, creator-led entertainment, documentaries, podcasts and other specialty programming, including eCLUTCH (exclusive) and more.” 

The company says it will add new content over time and expand into other regions, starting with Canada.

Sony has been late in introducing a FAST service, and follows in the footsteps of successful offerings such as Roku Channel, Fox’s Tubi and Sling Freestream. Sony’s previous live TV service was the subscription-based PlayStation Vue, a competitor to YouTube TV and Sling, and it shut down in 2019.

title: Apple pundits say Vision Pro is by far the best way to watch baseball
snippet: Both Apple pundits and most of the internet seem to agree that Vision Pro is the best way to watch baseball, following the immersive experience offered by Apple’s Friday Night Baseball. Notably, there also seemed to be a consensus view that less is more when it comes to the various immersive camera angles … more…
fullText:
Both Apple pundits and most of the internet seem to agree that Vision Pro is the best way to watch baseball, following the immersive experience offered by Apple’s Friday Night Baseball.

Notably, there also seemed to be a consensus view that less is more when it comes to the various immersive camera angles …

Macworld’s Michael Simon got the headline award with Apple finally hits the VR home run.

I’ve never had a desire to buy a Vision Pro. Even if I had $4,000 to blow at the Apple Store, I’d probably pick up a loaded MacBook Pro or a Mac mini with a Studio Display XDR instead of Apple’s cutting-edge handset. But Friday Night Baseball in Apple Immersive changed my perspective. The first-ever broadcast of a live Major League Baseball game with 3D video recorded in 8K with a 180-degree field of view, watching the Red Sox-Yankees game on the Vision Pro was almost as breathtaking as being at Yankee Stadium.

Daring Fireball’s John Gruber was every bit as enthusiastic.

The whole thing was legit exciting. Vision Pro continues to get a bad rap because Apple hasn’t sold many of them, and isn’t going to sell many of them until they come out with new models that are cheaper and lighter and less fussy. But there’s no denying that these immersive experiences are fucking cool. And an immersive live experience adds something else. It’s ineffable. Hard to say why, but feeling like you’re at another place watching something happen live is magic. Just a few years ago it would have required literal magic. It wasn’t possible. Now it is.

Jason Snell at Six Colors was more restrained in his phrasing, but was also a fan.

In the end, it felt much more like I was sitting at Yankee Stadium watching the game. 

He said one change Apple made over its basketball footage was not cutting between lots of different camera angles, and he fully approved. Others agreed with him.

Each half inning was shown from a single camera on the dugout rail next to the on-deck circle, giving a great view of pitcher and hitter and the infield, as well as the goings on right in front of the dugout in foul territory. The camera switched between innings, so you were always viewing from the perspective of the at-bat team’s dugout. Making it all work better was Apple’s addition of a “virtual jumbotron” floating in the sky, a scoreboard with graphics and a video feed of the standard 16:9 telecast on Apple TV. It was easy to look up and catch a replay or even get a better view of something happening in the far-off outfield, without getting in the way of my view of the game itself.

Having watched a clip posted on X by Justin Ryan of Spatial Insider, this does seem to offer the best of both worlds.

Live immersive MLB on Apple Vision Pro. It felt like I was at Yankee Stadium. The whole experience was incredible.

Shot through the lens with iPhone since it can’t be recorded on headset. pic.twitter.com/oF1J9tBTd8

— Justin Ryan (@justinryanio) August 29, 2026

As someone who thinks a far less expensive and massively lighter face monitor is a better bet for most TV and movie viewing, I can definitely see the appeal of Vision Pro for this type of fully immersive experience. I’m still waiting for my perfect compromise product.

title: Mozilla launches ad blocking for Firefox on iOS
snippet: Mozilla is officially launching ad blocking for Firefox on iOS today, after testing the feature over the past few weeks. The new built-in option will block most third-party ads and trackers before they load on an iPhone, reducing bandwidth use and decluttering mobile websites. Mozilla is using Apple's WebKit Content Blocker technology and the EasyList filter to block ads in Firefox on iOS, so you won't need to download and install a separate extension to get it working. The ad blocking is controlled in the settings of Firefox on iOS, and Mozilla is keeping it disabled by default so you have to enable it from settings > browsing > ad blocker … Read the full story at The Verge.
fullText:
Tom Warren

 

is a senior correspondent and author of Notepad, who has been covering all things Microsoft, PC, and tech for over 20 years.

Mozilla is officially launching ad blocking for Firefox on iOS today, after testing the feature over the past few weeks. The new built-in option will block most third-party ads and trackers before they load on an iPhone, reducing bandwidth use and decluttering mobile websites.

Mozilla is using Apple’s WebKit Content Blocker technology and the EasyList filter to block ads in Firefox on iOS, so you won’t need to download and install a separate extension to get it working. The ad blocking is controlled in the settings of Firefox on iOS, and Mozilla is keeping it disabled by default so you have to enable it from settings > browsing > ad blocker. You can also toggle it on or off during a browsing session from the site menu option.

Not every ad will be blocked, though. Mozilla says ads served directly by a website or ads shown in search results will still appear. Unsurprisingly, sponsored shortcuts and other sponsored content shown by Firefox when you open a new tab won’t be blocked, either.

While this is the first time Firefox has gained ad blocking support on iOS, there are plenty of rival browsers that already offer similar support. Brave, Vivaldi, Opera, and others also have built-in ad blockers on iOS.

title: AAPL gained 2,736% under Cook, but Ternus doesn’t have to emulate him
snippet: Bloomberg carries a piece noting the astonishing gains made by Apple stockholders during the time when Tim Cook was CEO. The cumulative gain was 2,275% – or a total return of 2,736% when accounting for dividend payments also. The site suggests this will make him a tough act to follow, but my own view is that new CEO John Ternus doesn’t have to emulate Cook’s management of the company … more…
fullText:
Bloomberg carries a piece noting the astonishing gains made by Apple stockholders during the time when Tim Cook was CEO. The cumulative gain was 2,275% – or a total return of 2,736% when accounting for dividend payments also.

The site suggests this will make him a tough act to follow, but my own view is that new CEO John Ternus doesn’t have to emulate Cook’s management of the company … 

There’s no disputing the numbers Bloomberg cites.

Cook inherited a company with a market capitalization of less than $350 billion and built the maker of iPhones and Mac computers into a diverse $4.6 trillion business that also sells watches, AirPods and financial services […] During his time as CEO, the shares climbed a whopping 2,736% on a total-return basis.

But my stance is that John Ternus shouldn’t for one moment worry about whether Apple will emulate this degree of financial success under his leadership – and there are two reasons for this.

First, both of his key predecessors argued that financial success is a side effect of the true goal, not something that should be chased directly. Steve Jobs famously said:

“If you focus on making really great products, then the profits will follow.”

Cook himself has echoed this philosophy, saying that he never worried about quarterly results, but instead focused on the long-term direction of the company.

Second, the advice Steve gave to Tim when he took over:

“Don’t ask what I would do. Just do the right thing.”

Ternus shouldn’t ask himself what either Jobs or Cook would have done. He should instead  run Apple in the way that he thinks is most likely to see the successful development of the best possible products, and the evolution of the best company culture and values for long-term success. 

I suspect he will be a very different CEO to Cook, just as Cook was to Jobs. The goal isn’t to try to emulate past formulae, but instead to look ahead and – to borrow a phrase from the outgoing CEO – follow his own North Star.

iPhone 18 Pro will be unveiled on September 9, and a new report says pre-orders for the device will kick off slightly later than usual.

iPhone 18 Pro pre-orders likely starting Saturday, September 12

Apple announced this week that its big iPhone event will happen on Wednesday, September 9.

Normally, the company follows a very predictable schedule for fall iPhone launches. After the event, pre-orders usually open on Friday of that same week, with devices shipping the following Friday.

But we’re expecting a slightly different plan this year, and a new report corroborates the change.

This year, the ‘normal’ pre-order day would fall on Friday, September 11. The last time that a typical iPhone pre-order day happened on September 11, Apple pushed pre-orders back a day to Saturday, September 12.

It might be even more inclined than usual to do that again this year, as 2026 is the 25th anniversary of the 9/11 attacks.

Macwelt, the German companion to Macworld, says they’ve received a tip from a reliable source that iPhone 18 Pro pre-orders will indeed start on Saturday, September 12. The report adds:

The time is also set to change, according to the source: While pre-orders usually begin at 5 am PT, Apple is reportedly opening up pre-sales at midnight PT on Saturday.

The publication did incorrectly report the iPhone 17e’s release date earlier this year. So while September 12 does seem likely, the specific details around start time could be off.

title: Ryan Breslow is raising up to $27M in pay-to-play bridge funding to save Bolt
snippet: The controversial founder of the checkout startup once valued at $11 billion is putting in $5 million of his own money.
fullText:
Ryan Breslow, the controversial entrepreneur who returned as CEO of Bolt last year after years of legal battles and clashes with investors, refuses to give up on the checkout processing startup he co-founded in 2014.

The company, which hit an $11 billion valuation in early 2022 before plummeting 97% to $300 million, is now raising a bridge round of up to $27 million, Breslow told TechCrunch. Bridge rounds are short-term financings meant to tide a company over until its next major fundraise.

The capital is being raised from existing investors and structured as a convertible note, meaning it will turn into equity at a discount once Bolt closes a future funding round. It also includes a punitive “pay-to-play” provision, meaning backers who don’t participate will lose a large portion of their equity in the company.

Although Breslow didn’t frame it as such, the new financing may be the company’s last shot at survival. “This financing allows us to capitalize on our recent operational milestones, clear legacy obligations, and ensure a seamless transition as we progress toward the closing of our full Series E2 round,” according to a company press release. Breslow did not respond to requests for comment on what constitutes those legacy obligations.

Startups generally raise bridge financings in two situations: when they are performing well and need six to 12 months to hit their next milestone, or when they are running low on cash and need time to restructure or reach profitability.

Breslow declined to disclose how much cash Bolt has left, though he claimed the company is nearing profitability and returning to growth after years of shrinking revenue.

While it is not clear if Bolt is indeed running out of capital, Breslow is clearly determined to see the startup he founded 12 years ago, at age 19 as a Stanford dropout, survive. “I believe in Bolt more than anyone could possibly imagine. I believe Bolt is worth saving,” he told TechCrunch.

Breslow is personally committing $5 million to the round to demonstrate his belief in the company.

Whether Bolt’s backers share that confidence — and help it hit its fundraising target — remains to be seen. Breslow estimates that participation from Bolt’s roughly 100 investors will total at least $15 million, though he noted not everyone is expected to join in.

Breslow told TechCrunch shortly after being reinstated as Bolt’s CEO in March 2025 — three years after stepping down from the role — that he was in “early conversations” about a new round.

Ultimately, bringing the company to a point of a publicly announced fundraise took more than a year.

The new financing comes two years after Breslow attempted a $450 million round at a $14 billion valuation. That deal collapsed after existing investors, including BlackRock and Hedosophia, sued to block it, following revelations that one investor named as a lead backer of the round denied participating at all and another had offered $250 million in “marketing credits” instead of cash.  (The lawsuit was later voluntarily dismissed by all parties.)

Breslow says that unlike the failed $450 million round, Bolt’s board and a “majority of preferred” shareholders have signed off on the new fundraise. While he didn’t disclose how many of Bolt’s nearly 100 existing investors will double down, at least one angel backer, who asked not to be named, confirmed through his wealth manager that he plans to participate in the round.

Breslow maintains that Bolt would be in a much better position today had he continued running the company from 2022 to 2025, saying that the company lost customers when he was not at the helm.

He remains convinced he can restore Bolt to its former glory, telling TechCrunch, “I think we can be the Lyft to Stripe’s Uber.” Breslow is betting on the growth of the “super app” Bolt introduced last year, which integrates financial services, peer-to-peer payments, crypto, and credit cards into a one-click checkout.

Despite shrinking its headcount from 900 in 2021 to about 60 today, Breslow claims AI is allowing the company to operate far more efficiently. “We’re getting probably 10 times more done, shipping 10 times faster because of AI,” he said.

While running Bolt today is difficult, Breslow refuses to throw in the towel, arguing the company has a moat that would be impossible to replicate from scratch. Unlike other founders of fallen unicorns, Breslow isn’t ready to walk away and launch something new, even though he has been offered that option.

“I have friends who said, ‘Ryan, I’ll give you $10 million to start a new company. You don’t have to deal with this turnaround and this nightmare of a situation with Bolt,’” Breslow said.

Marina Temkin is a venture capital and startups reporter at TechCrunch. Prior to joining TechCrunch, she wrote about VC for PitchBook and Venture Capital Journal. Earlier in her career, Marina was a financial analyst and earned a CFA charterholder designation.

title: M6 Mac mini: Three things Apple didn’t highlight in the announcement
snippet: A new Mac mini with M6 and M5 Pro was unveiled this week, but we’ve since learned three things about the product that weren’t highlighted by Apple. more…
fullText:
A new Mac mini with M6 and M5 Pro was unveiled this week, but we’ve since learned three things about the product that weren’t highlighted by Apple.

#1: Memory bandwidth varies among configurations

If you’re planning to order a Mac mini, the pre-order page doesn’t tell the full story about a key spec: memory bandwidth. Digging into the technical specs reveals that your RAM choice might directly impact overall memory bandwidth.

The base M6 Mac mini with 16GB of RAM offers 153GB/s memory bandwidth. But if you upgrade to 24GB or 32GB of RAM, that number bumps up to 170GB/s.

Meanwhile, you’ll need to choose M5 Pro to get the maximum memory bandwidth of 307GB/s.

Every configuration is still an improvement over the M4 models, but it’s worth noting the differences.

#2: N1 chip brings Thread support

When Apple announced the new Mac mini, it highlighted Wi-Fi 7 and Bluetooth 6 support. Both are upgrades from the M4 model’s Wi-Fi 6E and Bluetooth 5.3.

But digging into the technical specs reveals that the M6 Mac mini includes an Apple-designed N1 chip. As a result, the Mac mini also has Thread support.

Thread has been part of the iPhone since the iPhone 15 Pro, with Apple touting its benefits for smart home accessories and automation. But it’s new to the Mac mini.

#3: macOS Golden Gate is preinstalled

If you try to avoid installing new macOS versions right away, it’s worth knowing that the M6 Mac mini ships with macOS Golden Gate.

Apple doesn’t explicitly say that anywhere on its website. However, the company reportedly confirmed to John Gruber that the new version of macOS is preinstalled.

This isn’t too surprising, since the M6 Mac mini won’t ship until September 22. macOS 27 will likely be released the week beforehand—on or around September 14. But anyone uneasy about upgrading to the latest software should take note.

For a full rundown of everything new in the M6 Mac mini vs the M4 model, see our overview here.

title: WhatsApp rolls out new chat themes on iOS, including animated wallpapers
snippet: Following the recent discovery that WhatsApp was working on new chat themes, the feature is now rolling out to iPhone users. Here are the details. more…
fullText:
Following the recent discovery that WhatsApp was working on new chat themes, the feature is now rolling out to iPhone users. Here are the details.

WhatsApp’s new chat themes include animated backgrounds

As reported by WABetaInfo, WhatsApp is now rolling out five new categories for chat themes: Featured, Nature, Live, Minimal, and Doodle. Just two weeks ago, the site had spotted references to the new theme galleries in code.

Image: WABetaInfo

The site notes that while Featured includes “a selection of the best themes available,” curated by WhatsApp’s design team, the Nature category “offers themes that bring outdoor landscapes to the chat screen.” Live, meanwhile,“features wallpapers that move slowly in the background,” while Minimal themes “apply a plain background to the chat screen: white in light mode and dark in dark mode.” Finally, Doodle includes WhatsApp’s classic wallpaper with the doodle patterns.

Here’s WABetaInfo on the Live wallpapers, which are arguably the most notable addition:

Live is the most distinctive category for this update. This category features wallpapers that move slowly in the background. WhatsApp marks these themes by a small Live icon in the top right corner of its thumbnail. This makes it easier for users to recognize themes with an animated wallpaper, even when they are listed into the Featured category. About the animation, WhatsApp keeps it deliberately slow, just enough to give the background a dynamic feel. This is important since a faster animation would distract users from reading their messages. It could also cause discomfort for people with certain accessibility needs. As a result, this is not a technical limitation, but it is a perfect design choice.

WABetaInfo notes that WhatsApp automatically assigns a chat bubble color based on the selected theme, and adds that, as is the case with WhatsApp rollouts, the new feature might not be immediately available to all users.

title: Google Keep for Android rolls out ‘Find in note’ search
snippet: The last big update to Google Keep was at the start of this year with the reminders-Tasks migration. Google has now updated Keep for Android with “Find in note” search. more…
fullText:
The last big update to Google Keep was at the start of this year with the reminders-Tasks migration. Google has now updated Keep for Android with “Find in note” search.

Open a note and tap the three-dot overflow menu in the bottom-right corner for the new option. “Find in note” appears at the top of this list and gives you straightforward text search.

title: OpenAI renews push to get Apple’s trade secret theft lawsuit tossed
snippet: Chang Liu, Tang Tan, OpenAI, and io Products filed a new petition asking the court to dismiss Apple’s trade secret misappropriation complaint with prejudice. Here’s what that means. more…
fullText:
Chang Liu, Tang Tan, OpenAI, and io Products filed a new petition asking the court to dismiss Apple’s trade secret misappropriation complaint with prejudice. Here’s what that means.

A bit of context

A few weeks ago, Apple filed a lawsuit accusing two former employees of trade secret misappropriation.

The lawsuit, which also includes OpenAI and Jony Ive’s io Products, claims that Chang Liu and Tang Tan took or accessed confidential Apple information after leaving the company, and that they coached prospective hires on how to avoid triggering Apple’s security systems while taking company information with them.

Apple has also been seeking a preliminary injunction to stop OpenAI and the other defendants from accessing, using, or disclosing Apple’s alleged proprietary information while the case proceeds, as well as expedited discovery to more quickly determine the scope of the alleged misappropriation (which would in turn also inform the scope of the injunction).

Following Apple’s filing, OpenAI and the other defendants responded by asking the court to dismiss the lawsuit, claiming that Apple had failed to clear the legal bars required to support its trade secret misappropriation claims.

They claim that Apple failed to identify protectable trade secrets with enough specificity, failed to plausibly allege that any of the defendants misappropriated them, and failed to show any resulting injury or ongoing harm.

Apple, in turn, responded by arguing that its complaint identifies specific trade secrets and specific acts of alleged misappropriation, while accusing the defendants of relying on unrelated events to offer innocent explanations for conduct Apple says it never alleged.

One example is OpenAI’s claim that Tang Tan retained Apple’s offboarding document only to help ensure that future hires complied with Apple’s security requirements, while another is its argument that Chang Liu accessed Apple information after leaving Apple because former colleagues had asked him for help.

Now, OpenAI has filed a new brief reaffirming its earlier arguments and asking the court to dismiss the lawsuit with prejudice, which would prevent Apple from bringing the same claims again in the future.

OpenAI renews push to dismiss lawsuit

In its new filing, OpenAI says Apple’s rebuttal to its motion to dismiss the lawsuit “confirms, rather than cures, the Complaint’s central defect,” arguing the following:

To state a DTSA claim, Apple must connect three propositions concerning the same information and the same Defendant: what the particular asserted trade secret is; why that information qualifies for protection; and how a defendant improperly acquired, disclosed, or used it. Neither Apple’s Complaint nor its opposition ever completes that chain. Apple’s supposed “trade secrets” are and remain vague categories and catch-alls, and Apple cannot substitute attorney characterization for missing facts.

OpenAI also accuses Apple of asking the court to “infer essential facts that are not alleged,” adding that while “Rule 12 permits reasonable inferences from alleged facts,” it “does not permit speculation to substitute for the missing act of misappropriation.”

A request that a candidate bring “parts” becomes assumed receipt of confidential information. Pre-interview downloading becomes assumed disclosure during the interview. A question about an Apple project becomes assumed receipt of trade-secret information. And allegations concerning one person somehow become acquisition or use by another.

Throughout its rebuttal, OpenAI essentially doubles down on the following arguments:

Apple fails to identify the alleged trade secrets

The complaint fails to identify any trade secrets

Apple fails to plead reasonable measures to protect its trade secrets

Apple fails to plead misappropriation by Chang Liu

Apple fails to plead misappropriation by Tang Tan

Apple fails to plead misappropriation by OpenAI or io Products

Apple fails to plead harm

The court should also dismiss Apple’s state law claims

With OpenAI’s motion to dismiss, Apple’s opposition, and OpenAI’s response now filed, briefing on the motion is effectively complete ahead of a hearing scheduled for October 1.

You can read OpenAI’s full motion below:

title: Google launches Gemini 3.5 Transcribe, which powers Gboard Rambler & is coming to Chrome
snippet: Google today introduced Gemini 3.5 Transcribe as its “most precise speech-to-text model yet” that is already powering several first-party products. more…
fullText:
Google today introduced Gemini 3.5 Transcribe as its “most precise speech-to-text model yet” that is already powering several first-party products.

Gemini Live gets productivity upgrade with Spark, Gmail, and other integrations 

Unlike conventional speech recognition models that struggle with background noise, complex jargon, and disfluency cleanup, Gemini 3.5 Transcribe converts raw audio directly into accurate, polished, formatted text.

This model is “designed to capture your natural speaking style to better understand your intent and recognize custom vocabulary.” As seen in Rambler, Gemini 3.5 Transcribe can handle self-corrections (“let’s meet Tuesday—no, Wednesday”) and remove “ums,” “ahs,” and other filler words from the end result, as well as auto-format your text and allow for natural voice editing. Additionally, Google touts:

More precise transcription: As measured by Artificial Analysis, achieves an average Word Error Rate (WER) of 4.0% for streaming and 2.6% for non-streaming use-cases. It shows strong performance across noisy, real-world environments, accurately capturing alphanumeric entities like postal codes and order IDs.

Custom vocabulary: Recognizes specialized jargon and unique spellings by seamlessly adapting transcriptions to your provided custom vocabulary.

Global language support: Automatically detects and transcribes over 85 languages, seamlessly handling regional accents and diverse dialects.

Multi-speaker identification: Accurately attributes speech in pre-recorded audio with timestamps for up to three speakers (support for 3+ speakers is experimental).

Performance-wise, Gemini 3.5 Transcribe offers what Google calls a “major advancement” across capabilities, improved word error rates, and significantly better latency over its Chirp 3 transcription model from 2025.

	

As measured by Artificial Analysis, time to final transcription, for example, improves by 70%. On the FLEURS benchmark across a set of top languages and locales, the model delivers precise multilingual performance, improving over Chirp 3, and achieving a 5.50% WER in streaming mode and 5.04% WER in non-streaming use-cases.

The other goal is to let you “execute tasks with your voice.” Function calling allows Gemini 3.5 Transcribe to “delegate complex tasks (such as image generation and file analysis) to other Gemini models.” This can be seen with the Speak to Window capability in the Gemini app for macOS.

Besides the Gemini macOS app and Gboard Rambler on Android, Gemini 3.5 Transcribe is available in Google Antigravity’s prompt box microphone where it “pairs screen context and chat history, with your permission, to ensure pinpoint transcription accuracy across file names, agent thoughts, and active documents.”

It’s coming next to the Chrome browser so you can “talk to type in any web field — making it effortless to dictate replies, draft posts, or prompt Gemini in Chrome more naturally and easily with your voice.”

Gemini 3.5 Transcribe is available:

For developers: In public preview in the Gemini API via Google AI Studio and Google Antigravity.

For enterprises: In public preview via Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform and coming soon to Gemini Enterprise for Customer Experience.

title: Apple Pay is getting even better with four new features and more
snippet: Apple Pay is a go-to feature for iPhone users when shopping in stores, online, and in apps. Apple recently announced four new features that make Apple Pay even better. Here’s how they work, plus one major expansion that’s rolling out now. more…
fullText:
Apple Pay is a go-to feature for iPhone users when shopping in stores, online, and in apps. Apple recently announced four new features that make Apple Pay even better. Here’s how they work, plus one major expansion that’s rolling out now. 

New design in iOS 27

One of my favorite changes in iOS 27 is the redesigned Apple Pay checkout interface. The new interface makes it much easier to switch between different cards during the checkout flow on websites and in apps.

In the new design, you can easily swipe between cards on the main Apple Pay checkout screen. You can also tap on a card to view a grid of all your available Apple Pay cards.

The design also makes it easier to see information about individual cards, including rewards, balances, pay later options, and more.

iOS 27 is available in beta to developers and public beta users. It will be released to everyone this fall.

American Express rewards

Apple and American Express recently announced a new partnership that lets you pay with American Express rewards points.

When shopping online or in apps with an American Express card, you’ll see a new “Use Rewards” option alongside your available Membership Rewards points balance. You can apply points to cover all or part of your purchase, right in the Apple Pay checkout flow.

American Express points redeemed via Apple Pay are valued at 0.7 cents each. For example, this means 10,000 points can be redeemed for $70 applied towards your purchase.

In iOS 27, Apple is adding a new “Tap to Share” feature that integrates with Apple Pay on iPhone for in-store shopping.

This feature, which Apple says will launch this fall, is an extension of Tap to Pay on iPhone. Apple explains:

With just a tap, customers can connect to a participating merchant’s iPhone for a more personalized and faster in-store purchase experience that allows for secure sharing of information, such as email and other contact information, shipping address, loyalty rewards information, and more.

Customers will also be able to view the items in their basket in real time so they can keep track of what they’ve purchased and ensure all sales and discounts are properly applied.

When done, shoppers can complete the checkout on their iPhone using Apple Pay.

Reload debit cards

Later this year, iPhone users will be able to manage their debit card balances directly in the Apple Pay interface.

According to Apple, you’ll be able to use Apple Pay to add money to a supported debit card directly in Apple Wallet or when checking out.

Bonus: Apple Pay at Walmart 

This one isn’t really a new feature developed by Apple. Instead, it’s something that should’ve happened years ago finally coming to fruition. Walmart has announced that it is finally starting to roll out support for Apple Pay. Apple Pay is also rolling out to Sam’s Club as part of this initiative.  

Walmart started rolling out Apple Pay (and broader contactless support) this week in Arkansas. The retailer says it launch for all stores in the United States by the end of this year. 

Wrap up

As Apple Pay continues to increase in popularity and prevalence among retailers, it’s great to see Apple continue to improve the experience. Personally, Apple Pay is my checkout payment method of choice basically everywhere I shop — whether that’s online or in store.

How often do you use Apple Pay? What are your favorite Apple Pay features? Let us know down in the comments.

title: Just How Water-Resistant Is Apple’s iPhone? I Tested It in My Swimming Pool
snippet: Take a look back at Apple’s first water-resistant iPhone and how we made it Jacques Cousteau for a day with our underwater tests.
fullText:
There’s nothing I love more than testing a tech company’s claims. I used to host a CNET YouTube series called Breaking Point, where I got to do what most people try to avoid: torture their tech. That meant purposely dropping thousands of dollars’ worth of phones on the ground, dunking them in water and pushing them to their limits. 

So when Apple released its first water-resistant iPhone in 2016, I thought, “Game on!”

It’s hard to imagine now, but before the iPhone 7, a splash of water could make your Apple phone useless. Its IP67 rating means it can withstand 30 minutes in 1 meter of water (about 3 feet). To test it, I took the iPhone 7 for a “swim” in the pool at my old San Francisco apartment building, along with then CNET senior editor Sean Hollister, and filmed the whole thing.

We ended up testing it beyond its limits and didn’t exactly follow all the care instructions. Spoiler alert: The iPhone mostly survived, but it did come away with a battle scar or two.

At the time, I was blissfully unaware that just because a phone is fine after being underwater doesn’t mean it escaped damage. Chlorinated pool water and ocean saltwater can slowly corrode the materials inside a phone, even after it’s dried out. That wouldn’t kill a phone right away, but it would shorten its lifespan. Water damage (intentional or not) will void Apple’s warranty. 

Looking back at this 10-year-old video of Hollister and me throwing an iPhone 7 into a pool is ironic. Instead of taking my phone on more water-related adventures, safe in the knowledge that my tech should be fine, I’m careful with my iPhone around water. Less fun, yes, but more informed.

Watch my full Did the iPhone 7 Survive Our Water Test? video down below.

title: The Wickedly Easy Ways Smart Thermostats Tackle Home Humidity Problems
snippet: If you struggle with high humidity or dry air, you may be surprised what today’s advanced thermostats can do to help. Here’s how I use mine.
fullText:
I wouldn’t wish humidity problems on anyone’s home. On the dry side, low humidity can cause everything from nosebleeds to cracks in dried-out wood flooring. And high humidity can encourage mold, warp wood or damage paint. Depending on how delicate your houseplants are, both extremes could also threaten their health.

But the smart thermostat, that unsung hero of the modern home, has hidden potential to fix this problem. These thermostats not only help gauge humidity, but they can automatically take action to prevent issues or alert you so you can maintain just the right indoor air quality. Here’s how to get started.

Yes, the right thermostat really can sense humidity

Today’s smart thermostats, including the Google Nest, have humidity sensors.

Google

Quick, what’s the humidity in your house right now? Most households don’t know, certainly not by checking traditional thermostats and definitely not when they’re away from home. Smart thermostats are different.

Today’s smart thermostats, including some of our favorite models like the Ecobee Premium and Google Nest thermostats, have built-in humidity sensors that are always detecting moisture in the air of your home. With the app on your phone, including popular platforms like Google Home and Alexa, you can check on humidity levels at any time, no matter where you are, before problems begin emerging.

With a smart thermostat, you can check humidity and get alerts from anywhere.Tyler Lacoma/CNET

Some thermostats even allow you to set alerts when humidity levels reach certain thresholds, so your phone will tell you when you need to take action. Humidity isn’t always related to temperature, either. When I asked Dan Bereiter, senior product manager of Honeywell Home Solutions at Residio, about these features, he advised a combo approach. “If the temperature looks comfortable, but the home still feels stuffy, clammy, or dry, humidity may be part of the issue. Watching both temperature and humidity can help homeowners make more informed adjustments.”

What if your smart thermostat doesn’t have a humidity sensor? That’s easy to address.

You can hook up a humidity sensor to nearly any smart thermostat

Thermostat satellite sensors are one of the best inventions for home heating.

Tyler Lacoma/CNET

I’ve experimented with an array of sensors that can measure humidity, from all-purpose versions from SwitchBot to the Wyze room sensor, the capable Aqara sensor and even an affordable humidity sensor from Ikea.

All these sensors can provide humidity readings to your thermostat, or independently to their own apps, which can still supply alerts to your phone about certain humidity levels. Many can also work with broader smart home platforms that can combine multiple devices like Google Home, Apple Home and Alexa, which can make it even easier to connect to thermostats and other devices.

With a press of this Ikea button, you can see the nearby temperature and humidity.

Tyler Lacoma/CNET

In some ways these smaller devices are even more useful than built-in humidity sensors, because you can move them to whichever room has the worst humidity problems, or the most delicate plants, etc., to get more accurate readings.

Then humidity levels can automatically turn on appliances

Humidifiers are easy to find at major retailers and are sold at a variety of price points.

MistAire via Amazon

With a smart humidity sensor, it’s now easy to set up a routine to let your house automatically tackle humidity problems. One of the best ways to do this is with a smart humidifier or dehumidifier. These include features that can connect to smart home platforms, too, which means you can set up an easy rule: “If the humidity reaches a certain level, turn on the humidifier/dehumidifier.”

What indoor humidity levels are best? Bereiter told me: “The EPA recommends maintaining indoor relative humidity (RH) between 30% and 50% because balanced humidity can help improve comfort, support HVAC system efficiency, and help protect building materials from excess moisture.”

You can set up a rule like this in just a couple of minutes, usually under the “Automations” section. The hardest part is connected sensors and appliances to Wi-Fi and adding them to apps, but as long as you have a reliable Wi-Fi router nearby, this shouldn’t be a problem.

These automations works best for larger models that can quickly adjust humidity, but of course the biggest will need to be refilled with water, or need a way to empty the water they’ve collected from the air (some use window units with a hose going outside). There are also whole-house dehumidifiers with smart capabilities by companies like AprilAire and TCL, as well as ways to connect to whole-house units with thermostats like Ecobee’s.

Of course, these smart appliances can get pricey. If you want to save money or already have a humidity device, you can usually make it smart by connecting it to a smart plug. These smart plugs can turn humidifiers/dehumidifiers on or off based on schedules and rules you set up in apps. Smart plugs are only around $10 to $15, so it’s a very cheap way to add smart features to an appliance you already have.

If you do want to add a smart plug to your appliance, double-check it can function with basic on/off commands. Not all humidifiers, for example, turn on correctly when controlled by a smart plug. I suggest scanning reviews online to see if anyone has tried using the appliance or a model from the same brand with a smart plug to make sure it works before you buy.

Some thermostats can even tap directly into AC and heat pumps

Cooling and humidity settings are more advanced then ever and can connect to current home systems.Tyler Lacoma/CNET

Setting up rules to automatically turn on humidifiers or dehumidifiers is an excellent use of the smart home, and your plants, pets, family and lungs will benefit. But many smart thermostats can do even more.

Thermostat models also have the ability to connect to supported air conditioner systems and heat pumps (they don’t even have to be smart). These systems can act as natural dehumidifiers when they turn on, so it’s an easy way to lower humidity and heat in a home when they become problematic.

One of my favorite versions is Google Nest’s Cool to Dry, because it’s nearly effortless to turn on and can work with any AC or heat pump as long as you have the right wiring – follow the link to learn more about the details. Nest even takes it a step further with its new thermostat capability Humidity Helper, which taps into existing humidifiers/dehumidifiers to automatically set up rules for you.

Honeywell Home smart thermostats can also connect to AC and humidity features, particularly Resideo systems. AprilAire also offers a whole home setup that allows smart thermostats to control AC, air purifiers and more. Remember, if these setups get too complicated for you, you can always contact an HVAC professional to connect everything for you or find out what your home supports.

Even without automations set up, you can still take action

Do all these smart connections and automations feel like too much? Don’t want to spend any more money on appliances? You don’t have to use them to improve humidity levels. Take manual action and use your thermostat’s humidity readings to make decisions about when to open windows, turn on your AC, flip on a humidifier and so on. More information from your thermostat means better decisions for your home, no matter how you go about it.

Humidity changes can even help you save money

Humidity management could even lead to savings.Tyler Lacoma/CNET

Humidity has such a big influence on how we feel at home, dealing with it may mean running your heating or cooling system less and potentially saving money. 

“High humidity can make a home feel warmer than it actually is, often leading homeowners to lower the thermostat and forcing the AC system to work harder,” Bereiter warned me. 

A combination of smart thermostat suggestions and eco modes, plus taking care of humidity, may be able to make your home feel cooler while also saving on your energy bills. However, be careful. Constantly using your AC or humidifier to control humidity can have the opposite effect and cost more energy, so work on hitting the sweet spot for savings.

Final note: Humidity can change significantly between seasons in some climates. Certain setups may work best in winter if your cold season is especially dry, or you may only need a humidifier setup in sweltering summers. Either way, smart thermostats and sensors can help out.

		

				

					

						

													

					

					

						

Tyler Lacoma
						

						

							Editor / Home Security and Smart Home						
					

											

				

											Tyler has worked on, lived with and tested all types of smart home and security technology for over a dozen years, explaining the latest features, privacy tricks, and top recommendations.
With degrees in Business Management, Literature and Technical Writing, Tyler takes every opportunity to play with the latest AI technology, push smart devices to their limits and occasionally throw cameras off his roof, all to find the best devices to trust in your life. He always checks with the renters (and pets) in his life to see what smart products can work for everyone, in every living situation. 
Living in beautiful Bend, Oregon gives Tyler plenty of opportunities to test the latest tech in every kind of weather and temperature. But when not at work, he can be found hiking the trails, trying out a new food recipe for his loved ones, keeping up on his favorite reading, or gaming with good friends.

title: Google announces ‘Expert Intelligence’ to let you add Play Books in Gemini Notebook
snippet: Expert Intelligence is a new “cross Google initiative that helps you engage with your trusted sources through Google AI products,” starting with Play Books and Gemini Notebook. more…
fullText:
Expert Intelligence is a new “cross Google initiative that helps you engage with your trusted sources through Google AI products,” starting with Play Books and Gemini Notebook.

Select ebooks that you’ve purchased from Google Play Books can now be added to Gemini Notebook and used as sources. This lets you “ask questions about the book and receive responses grounded directly in that book.”

You can also generate Infographics, Audio Overviews, Quizzes, and other Gemini Notebook features from the book.

Another way to use Expert Intelligence is in combination with your information. For example:

	

A manager can ask Gemini Notebook to help brainstorm strategies on how to best give employees feedback and navigate tough conversations by consulting Kim Scott’s Radical Candor: Be a Kick-Ass Boss Without Losing Your Humanity.

A woman can securely upload her journal entries to a notebook that also includes The New Menopause, to better understand how Dr. Mary Claire Haver’s expertise applies to her own life, with direct citations to relevant content in her book.

A parent can take a picture of the items in their fridge and ask for help creating a healthy family meal plan for the week based on Michael Pollan’s Food Rules: An Eater’s Manual.

Expert Intelligence today is compatible with over 100,000 books from Bloomsbury, De Gruyter Brill, Johns Hopkins University Press, Macmillan Publishers, O’Reilly Media, and Penguin Random House. 

Google worked with authors and publishers on controls that ensure users “must own the book through Google Play Books” before they can interact with it. 

If a notebook is shared, other collaborators will be prompted to purchase their own copy to engage with the content further. Otherwise, the book will be unavailable within their notebook. We believe that over time, Expert Intelligence will create content discovery and help authors reach new and more engaged readers.

To check whether a title is eligible for Expert Intelligence, visit the Google Play Books listing.

If eligible, you’ll see Gemini Notebook listed when you click the “Tools” badge on a book’s detail page.

Looking ahead, you’ll be able to use Expert Intelligence in the Gemini app and AI Mode. Meanwhile, “people will also be able to add more sources like third-party subscriptions, business research reports, and textbooks.”

title: Report: Apple Watch Series 12 may feature always-on heart-rate tracking, new Fitness app
snippet: According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple has a couple new features in the pipeline for Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 that’ll make it much more appealing for health-conscious users. The company is also testing two finishes for the rumored ceramic version. more…
fullText:
According to Bloomberg’s Mark Gurman, Apple has a couple new features in the pipeline for Apple Watch Series 12 and Ultra 4 that’ll make it much more appealing for health-conscious users. The company is also testing two finishes for the rumored ceramic version.

New health upgrades

These two key health upgrades will likely sound appealing if you’re someone who’s dissatisfied with the state of Apple Watch as a fitness tracker. The two features are always-on heart-rate tracking, and an all new app design. that’ll make it much easier to learn from your health data. Here’s how Gurman describes the new app:

Apple is also working on revamping its fitness and health app software to show more wellness-related metrics in a similar fashion to increasingly popular app offerings from Whoop and Oura.

As someone who currently owns a WHOOP, I will say my primary draw to it has always been the fact that I find it much easier to learn from my health data in the WHOOP app. It’ll show me all of the factors that make my sleep or recovery poor, whereas with Apple Watch it feels the only important thing is your activity rings. If Apple makes meaningful progress in this regard, I’ll be quite happy.

A key part of making the Apple Watch a more data-rich experience is well, having more data. Apple is reportedly testing the ability for the heart-rate sensor to record all day, rather than only during workouts and at random.

Two new finishes

We’ve already heard that Apple is weighing ceramic for the Apple Watch Series 12, though Gurman is now reporting that there’ll be two color options: the traditional white, as well as a dark gray color. There’ll also be “many new band colors and configurations.”

Redesign in the future

The current Apple Watch design language was introduced in 2024, with the Apple Watch Series 12. It was a relatively modest shift, with the company making the watch much thinner at the compromise of bezels. According to Bloomberg, we may see a new Apple Watch redesign next year with the Series 13, though it could shift to the Series 14:

Apple is pushing to have a big redesign for its watch ready by next year, but things could still slip to the year after.

I am quite excited to see what Apple cooks up here. It does feel like they’ve about peaked at what they can do with the rounded off design language, so maybe we’ll see a new shape entirely. Hopefully it doesn’t break backwards compatibility with older watch bands.

fullText:
I’ve always been a bit skeptical of smart glasses and mixed reality headsets. It’s not hard to find the utility of something like a Meta Quest in gaming, but Apple’s Vision Pro, for example, has never appealed to me in the slightest. Ahead of its first pair of Android XR glasses, though, I’ve spent some time with the XREAL One Pro and two things have become immediately clear – this is the hardware that could make Android XR shine, and XREAL will benefit greatly from Android XR.

If you’re unfamiliar with XREAL, I actually can’t blame you one bit. I always knew about this company, but the idea of glasses that put a screen in front of my face never sounded particularly worthwhile to me. But when XREAL mentioned it would adopt Android XR, I just had to give this tech a shot.

So, lately, I’ve been using XREAL One Pro, plugged into either a Galaxy Z Fold 7, MacBook, or a Redmagic Astra 2 tablet. The idea is really that simple. Whatever you’re doing, just plug it into the glasses and see it pop up on a 157-inch display (customizable) in front of your face. Initially, I wasn’t all that sure I’d find it useful, but a clear use case did immediately come up – airplanes.

Having a giant screen that floats in front of you and follows your movements is just so perfect in that context. It sure beats a seatback screen, and wearing them for a few hours on a flight is pretty comfortable too.

	

I’d never do this with a full headset, it’s just too bulky and weird-looking. XREAL One Pro don’t exactly look “normal.” They stick out from your face a little too far to be subtle, but the compact size in your bag and the cable running down makes it pretty clear what’s going on. 

These still don’t look normal, but they’re way less goofy than a VR headset
This is so much easier to transport compared to a VR headset

As for the actual quality, it’s pretty great. Like any screen in front of your face, it takes a minute to dial in the settings, but movies look great once you do. Mirroring my MacBook screen also made a great full-size canvas to do some work, all without worrying about the person in front of me reclining and ruining the whole experience. It’s not perfect, as while XREAL’s 3DoF tracking is fantastic on the ground, it has a tendency to drift around while on a flight, especially if there’s any turbulence.

The only trouble comes from the unfortunate fact that not everything works. When plugged into the Redmagic tablet, for instance, I ran into problems with certain video apps including Fandango at Home and Google TV, though the latter worked fine on my Fold over DeX. The 3D conversion mode also never worked on the Redmagic tablet, though it was pretty solid when it did work on my Fold.

You can change how much of the real world you see, no cameras needed

And I think that’s where XREAL Aura with Android XR will “complete” the experience.

XREAL One Pro just builds on whatever you feed into it. The on-board controls and software are limited, and you simply can’t do anything without your secondary device. There are add-ons for gesture controls, and XREAL sells an Android phone that adds a UI to the glasses, but I think Android XR truly is the missing puzzle piece. XREAL seems to agree, as the company is pretty vocal about its vision for the future involving a lot more Android XR. And it’s not like the ability to plug in a device will go away, as Aura is set to support that.

There’s absolutely still space for what we have today. As mentioned, the simple ability to watch movies or get a bigger laptop display on the go rocks. But that’s where something like XREAL’s new A01+ glasses can shine, and for a lot less money at $299. I wouldn’t fork over $600 for XREAL One Pro just to get a bigger screen I can throw in my bag, but I’d definitely pay for the A01+, and XREAL 1S at $450 is also worth considering – I tried those out back at CES, and they work just about as well as One Pro, at least for the purposes I’ve mentioned here.

XREAL Aura is set to launch later this year, while One Pro, 1S, and A01+, are all available now.

Have you tried these out? Let us know your thoughts in the comments below.

title: Google Store error rejecting trade-in credits for Pixel 10 owners upgrading to Pixel 11
snippet: The Google Store seems to have an ongoing problem that is causing Pixel 11 upgraders to get a failed trade-in with removed credits when moving up from a Pixel 10. more…
fullText:
The Google Store seems to have an ongoing problem that is causing Pixel 11 upgraders to get a failed trade-in with removed credits when moving up from a Pixel 10.

While year-over-year upgrades aren’t for everyone, the Google Store’s solid trade-in values made upgrading from the Pixel 10 over to a Pixel 11 a pretty reasonable offer. 

Or, it would have.

Several Reddit threads have popped up in recent days (thanks Jules!) with prior Pixel 10 owners having gotten a notice from the Google Store that their trade-in had failed and their Pixel 11 upgrade just got a whole lot more expensive. Affected users have found that their initial trade-in value was accepted and processed for the full amount, only for the trade-in to be rejected now that the new device had been delivered and the old device shipped off. 

	

The email says that the trade-in device was “assessed” with an error description that an “Unknown or unsupported phone” was received. It sounds like Google’s trade-in partner was perhaps not set up to accept last year’s models, as this is happening solely with Pixel 10 series devices. Those affected are seeing credit card charges, devices being shipped back, or both. 

Clearly, there’s an issue on Google’s end here, but there’s no clear resolution at the moment. Support has told some users that there is a known issue, so it’s likely a fix is in the works. In the meantime, let us know in the comments below if you’ve run into this problem, and we’ll update this article if Google provides any further clarity on the situation.

title: Gemini Notebook switching to compute-based usage limits, like Gemini app
snippet: Following the Gemini app in May, Gemini Notebook is switching to “compute-specific usage limits” starting in September. more…
fullText:
Following the Gemini app in May, Gemini Notebook is switching to “compute-specific usage limits” starting in September.

Related: Google announces ‘Expert Intelligence’ to let you add Play Books in Gemini Notebook

This system replaces the set number of feature generations per day that depended on your Google AI tier. Limits refresh every five hours “rather than daily.” 

Google explains that “your overall usage limit will factor in prompt complexity, chat length, number of sources, and the features you use.” Notebooks will “help you keep track of your usage,” with a status appearing below the chat: 

“You’re almost at your AI usage limit. Limit resets at 3:00 PM.”

“Limit reached. All features are available after 3:00 PM.”

Another indicator will appear at the bottom of Studio generations to show expected AI usage cost: “The more the bar is filled in, the higher the expected cost.”

	

Gemini Notebook will “suggest alternative outputs if your first choice surpasses your limit.” There’s also “Generate later” to “defer generating outputs,” like intensive Video Overviews or Slide Decks. Google will automatically create them once your limit resets, with this feature coming first to the web. 

Free/Without a plan: Standard limits

Google AI Plus: 2x higher than standard limits

Google AI Pro: 4x higher than standard limits

Google AI Ultra: 5x or 20x higher than AI Pro depending on your subscription

The new compute-based usage limits will start rolling out to consumer accounts on web and mobile on September 2.

title: Oppo Find X10 ‘Pro Max’ reportedly gets three 200MP cameras
snippet: Oppo Find X10 isn’t too far away and, according to a new leak, a “Pro Max” model is going to ship with three 200MP cameras. more…
fullText:
Oppo Find X10 isn’t too far away and, according to a new leak, a “Pro Max” model is going to ship with three 200MP cameras.

While virtually every smartphone has a good camera now, Oppo is one of the brands pushing the envelope even further, with the Find X9 Ultra being one of the most impressive smartphone cameras in recent memory.

We’re approaching time for the Oppo Find X10 series and, right on cue, a new leak is delivering some new information. Ice Universe says that the Oppo Find X10 “Pro Max” will have three 200MP cameras on its back, and that’s notable for two reasons.

Of course, that starts with the simple fact that this is a phone with 600MP of camera sensors across its back, and that’s wild in itself. It’s also a massive upgrade over the trio of 50MP cameras on Find X9 Pro. Even Find X9 Ultra “only” had two 200MP sensors, with two more 50MP shooters finishing out the setup. Ice also mentioned that the main camera will use Samsung’s new ISOCELL HPC sensor.

	

The other tidbit in there is “Pro Max,” implying that Oppo is introducing a new variant to the Find X10 lineup. Last year, it maxed out at the Oppo Find X9 Pro. 

The Oppo Find X9 series launched in October 2025, both in China and globally, so we’re likely just a few weeks away from the Find X10’s debut.
